AI CLI Tools Community Digest 2026-11-09

Generated: 2026-11-09 00:44 UTC | Tools covered: 7

  • Claude Code
  • OpenAI Codex
  • Gemini CLI
  • GitHub Copilot CLI
  • OpenCode

Cross-Tool Comparison

AI CLI Tools — Cross-Tool Comparison Report

Date: 2026-11-09 · Tools: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Qwen Code

1. Ecosystem Overview

The AI CLI ecosystem on 2026-11-09 is in a consolidation-and-hardening phase: no tool shipped a stable release in the window, and community energy is concentrated in the issue trackers rather than on release notes. The dominant engineering concern has shifted from "can the agent do this?" to "can I trust it to do this repeatedly?" — session lifecycle integrity, context/compaction correctness, permission semantics, and cost/quota accounting dominate every tracker. A second, structural theme is agent governance: subagent hook policies, fail-closed guardrails, and per-thread authorization are being requested across Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, and Pi simultaneously. Meanwhile, platform-specific reliability — Windows sandboxing, macOS kernel panics, ARM64 packaging — is generating a disproportionate share of high-severity reports, suggesting desktop/client parity is the current weakest link.

2. Activity Comparison

Tool Issues (24h) PRs (24h) Discussions (24h) Releases (24h)
Claude Code ~50+ updated (#108479–#108486 newly filed) 0 N/A (no Discussions data) None
OpenAI Codex 50 9 (8 closed, 1 open) 8 (3 Ideas, 5 Show & tell) None
Gemini CLI ~30 tracked; 10 hot ~10 (2 closed, 8 open) N/A (no Discussions data) None
GitHub Copilot CLI 15 updated 0 (no PR data) N/A None
OpenCode Top-10 hot + cluster (~15+) ~10 N/A (forum-style issues only) None
Pi ~10 hot (mostly closed same-day) 4 (all closed) 2 (Show & tell) None
Qwen Code 50 updated; 30 visible 10 (1 closed, 9 open) N/A 3 releases (nightly CLI, TS SDK v0.1.30, Desktop v0.27.0)

Notes:

  • Qwen Code is the only tool with releases in the window — and notably, Desktop v0.27.0 immediately generated a P1 regression report (#16683, Intel x64 Mac crash). Fast iteration, immediate field feedback.
  • Pi had the highest triage throughput: nearly every hot issue and all 4 PRs moved to CLOSED within 24h, indicating a responsive maintainer loop.
  • Claude Code and Copilot CLI had zero PR activity — Claude Code is purely issue-tracker-driven today, while Copilot CLI's digest notes no PR data was available.
  • N/A vs. inactive: Per the source data, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, and Qwen Code provide no standalone Discussions data — these are marked N/A, not inactive.

3. Shared Feature Directions

Direction Tools Specific Need
Agent governance / programmable guardrails Codex (#60167 fail-closed subagent hook, #60307 per-thread Auto-review), Gemini CLI (#22672 discourage destructive git/DB ops, #19873 sandboxed bash), Copilot CLI (#5383 default agent config), Pi (#11932 auto_retry_decision hook), OpenCode (#62213 last-match-wins policy ordering) Policy enforcement at the agent/subagent boundary, not globally; hooks that can withhold/block results
Context economy & compaction correctness Claude Code (#85138, #82144 skill replay cost; #83756 MCP cache invalidation), Codex (#60293 empty compaction wipes history), OpenCode (#62778 compaction aborts turn; #62769 FTS session search), Pi (#10287 context overestimation; #10162 image-induced halts), Qwen Code (#16417 pre-flight write rejection; #16173 file-slice references) Compaction must not cause data loss, cost inflation, or silent turn aborts; token-budget awareness before action
Session lifecycle integrity Claude Code (#108238 nested side sessions), Codex (#37967 live session attach, #41708 Android queue), Copilot CLI (#5219 wedged session, #5100 ack timeout, #5380/#5382 extension init across create_session/new_context), OpenCode (#48826 subagent early completion, #62791/#62792 restart recovery), Pi (#11919 MCP reconnect blocking) A single transient failure must not permanently brick a long-running session
Subagent observability & correctness Gemini CLI (#22323 false-success on MAX_TURNS, #22598 surface trajectories in /chat share), OpenCode (#62793 stricter follow-up semantics), Codex (#60190 agent tree IDs), Claude Code (#108238) Accurate termination status; subagent trajectories visible in reports/shares; explicit follow-up vs. new-agent semantics
MCP reliability & observability Pi (#11918 OAuth headers lost, #11919 sequential reconnect blocking, #11921 tool_search misses, #10871 footer status), Gemini CLI (#24246 >128 tools → 400 error, #30071 OAuth TOCTOU fix), Copilot CLI (#4378 GHEC 401/403 silent drop), Claude Code (#83756 cache invalidation) Auth persistence across calls; non-blocking parallel reconnect; connection status surfaced in UI; tool-count scoping
Remote Control / cross-surface parity Codex (#37967, #41708, #60310 WSL reconnect), Claude Code (#102828 mobile→desktop handoff, #91874 plugin parity CLI↔web), OpenCode (#54375 preserve tab model) Live session attach across CLI/desktop/mobile; state and entitlements follow the user across surfaces
Terminal integration & observability Copilot CLI (#5320 OSC 7501, highest 👍 today), Gemini CLI (#29918 OSC 7501, closed), Qwen Code (#11929 Windows Terminal DECSET flicker) Native agent-status reporting so multiplexers (Herdr, etc.) can surface which session needs attention
Provider/model breadth & schema compatibility OpenCode (#23655 Responses API for Go, 👍31; #62786 Venice E2EE), Pi (#11936 Kimi root anyOf rejection, #11931 dropped native_finish_reason), Qwen Code (#16529 Wally as OpenAI-compatible) Parity across OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/local providers; robust normalization for OpenAI-compatible backends
Cost/quota transparency OpenCode (#59387 free tier, 333 comments; #62788 Claude plan usage to Console), Pi (#11857 prompt cache warming saved ~$1,430), Codex (#56866 5h limit drained in 10 min), Claude Code (#108238 weekly limits in ~1 day) Accurate quota accounting, visible spend, resets that actually fire
Enterprise/MCP configurability Copilot CLI (#4378 GHEC data residency), Codex (#60238–#60240 agent identity/permissions), Claude Code (#27302 multi-account Connectors, 453 👍) Multi-account/multi-identity support; verifiable agent authorization in third-party apps

4. Differentiation Analysis

Claude Code — issue-driven, trust-sensitive power users. Zero releases and zero PRs today; the tracker is dominated by high-engagement, long-lived issues (#27302 multi-account Connectors at 299 comments/453 👍, open since Feb). The pain profile is sophisticated: compaction/skill-replay side effects (a real unintended git push in #85138), cache invalidation contradicting docs (#83756), safety-classifier false positives in healthcare (#100212). Target user is a professional running long, skill-heavy, MCP-heavy sessions where correctness and cost are paramount.

OpenAI Codex — Windows hardening + remote-control coherence. Today's activity is split between Windows desktop reliability regressions (CreateProcessSecurityEnvironment 0x8007000F blocking trivial commands, powershell.exe polling, ~140 idle helpers leaked in 42h) and Remote Control state fragility across CLI/desktop/Android/WSL. Notably, Codex has the richest maintainer/bot PR cadence (8 closed internal PRs today) and the most active Discussions surface (8 items) — including three convergent proposals on agent identity/permissions (#60238–#60240), signaling enterprise aspirations.

Gemini CLI — security hardening + AST-aware codebase tooling. Gemini's PR stream today is unusually security-focused: a Windows git diff permission bypass (#30095), a CI secret-exposure gate for fork-controlled code (#30090, with a live PoC in #30066 and a forthcoming Google OSS VRP report), and an MCP OAuth TOCTOU fix (#30071). On the feature side, a coordinated AST-aware tooling cluster (#22745–#22747) targets token frugality and misaligned reads — a distinct technical bet on structural code understanding rather than raw context.

GitHub Copilot CLI — session/extension lifecycle reliability. The dominant theme is session bricking: a single bad subagent model id (#5219) or one 120s ack timeout (#5100) permanently wedges a long-running session. A cluster of extension/plugin bugs (#5380, #5381, #5382) shows headless/multi-session automation is not yet trustworthy. Highest-👍 items are ecosystem-integration requests (OSC 7501 at 👍11, Git Bash on Windows at 👍7), indicating users want Copilot CLI to fit existing terminal workflows rather than the reverse.

OpenCode — free-tier crisis + V2 subagent correctness. The free-tier master issue (#59387) at 333 comments is the single most acute community problem across all seven tools — resets that never fire, "all models blocked" states. Simultaneously, V2 subagent execution has a cluster of reproduced correctness bugs (early completion, restart recovery dropping notices, auto-compaction aborts on local providers). OpenCode is the only tool where local/self-hosted provider friction (Ollama compaction edge cases) is a top-tier pain point, and its PR stream shows ground-laying infra work (SQLite FTS5 session indexing, Venice E2EE, Claude plan usage reporting).

Pi — extension ecosystem + MCP reliability, with fast triage. Pi's differentiator is a mature extension API (requests for auto_retry_decision and ui_prompt_start hooks) and a maintainer team that closes issues same-day. Its pain clusters are MCP reliability (auth headers lost, blocking reconnects) and context-accounting correctness (#10287: 42k → 330k token jump after a network error). The #11857 prompt-cache-warming fix (~$1,430 saved, 26% of p2 spend) shows a cost-conscious user base and a team willing to optimize aggressively.

Qwen Code — CI stability drag + rapid release cadence. The only tool shipping releases today, but 9 of its top 30 issues are bot-filed CI/Managed Agent failures (#14724 at 277 comments — a monthly re-fire tracker). This is the project's single biggest operational drag. Its PR stream is substantive and infrastructure-oriented: MCP connection repair after aborted calls (#16661), provider HTTP status preservation in headless errors (#16686), ACP-managed skill scheduling (#16685), and partial-commit from Web Shell (#16681). Target user appears to be teams running managed/daemon sessions with GitHub channel integration.

5. Community Momentum & Maturity

By engagement volume:

  1. OpenCode — #59387 alone (333 comments) exceeds any single thread elsewhere; the free-tier crisis is driving massive community attention but also massive frustration.
  2. Claude Code — #27302 (299 comments, 453 👍) is the highest-👍 single issue across all tools; the tracker has deep, sophisticated engagement.
  3. Qwen Code — 50 issues updated in 24h, but heavily bot-generated; 277-comment CI tracker reflects re-fires, not discussion.
  4. OpenAI Codex — 50 issues + 9 PRs + 8 discussions; the most balanced multi-channel activity.
  5. Gemini CLI — ~30 tracked issues, security-focused PR momentum, high-upvote delegation bugs (#21409 at 👍8).
  6. GitHub Copilot CLI — 15 issues updated, zero PR activity; engagement is real but narrower.
  7. Pi — smallest raw volume but highest triage velocity; nearly all hot items closed same-day.

By iteration velocity:

  • Qwen Code iterates fastest on releases (3 today) but is dragged by CI instability.
  • OpenAI Codex shows the strongest maintainer-side PR cadence (8 closed internal PRs).
  • Pi shows the fastest issue-resolution loop.
  • Claude Code and Copilot CLI had no PR movement in the window — Claude Code is entirely issue-driven today, and Copilot CLI's zero-PR status may reflect reporting gaps.

By maturity signal:

  • Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Qwen Code show enterprise-adjacent concerns (GHEC data residency, agent identity, CI gates, managed-agent diagnostics) — mature enough that enterprise plumbing is now the friction.
  • Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi show power-user concerns (compaction correctness, cost accounting, extension APIs) — mature enough that users have built non-trivial workflows on top.
  • Pi is the most "extension-ecosystem-mature" relative to its size.

6. Trend Signals

1. Agent governance is the next platform battleground. Across Codex (#60167 fail-closed subagent hook, #60307 per-thread Auto-review), Gemini CLI (#22672 destructive-command discouragement, #19873 sandboxed bash), Copilot CLI (#5383 default agent config), and Pi (#11932 auto_retry_decision), the same ask recurs: policy enforcement at the agent boundary, with hooks that can withhold results before they enter parent context. Reference value: any tool shipping subagents should design for programmable, fail-closed governance now — retrofitting it later is painful, as Codex's four-month-open #31045 suggests.

2. Context management is the most fragile subsystem everywhere. Compaction data loss (Codex #60293), skill-replay side effects (Claude Code #85138 — a real unintended git push), context-usage overestimation (Pi #10287), compaction-aborts-turn on local providers (OpenCode #62778), and pre-flight write rejection (Qwen Code #16417) all point the same way. Reference value: treat compaction, skill replay, and context accounting as safety-critical infrastructure, not optimizations. The unintended-git push class of bug is a reputational risk, not just a bug.

3. Session lifecycle brittleness is a universal blocker for agentic workloads. One transient failure — a bad subagent model id (Copilot CLI #5219), a 120s ack timeout (#5100), a restart mid-turn (OpenCode #62791), a failed MCP read (Claude Code #108238) — can permanently degrade or brick a long-running session. Reference value: session recovery and idempotent resume are table stakes for anyone targeting "run indefinitely" workflows; Pi and Qwen Code are investing here (reconnect repair, restart terminalization), while Copilot CLI and OpenCode show the cost of not doing so.

4. Cost/quota transparency is a churn driver. The most-engaged threads across tools are about money and limits: OpenCode's free-tier master (333 comments), Claude Code's weekly-limits-in-a-day + kernel panic (#108238), Codex's 5h-limit-in-10-minutes (#56866), Pi's prompt-cache-warming ($1,430 saved). Reference value: inaccurate quota accounting and silent cost burn are not billing bugs — they are trust bugs. Pi's #11857 shows the upside: a targeted cache-warming fix delivered measurable savings and goodwill.

5. Windows and ARM64 desktop are the weakest platform links. Windows sandbox regressions (Codex #59941, #25453), Windows update locks (Qwen Code #15276), Windows Terminal flicker (#11929), Windows Git permission bypass (Gemini CLI #30095), ARM64 jemalloc crash (Copilot CLI #4977, now closed), and Intel x64 Mac desktop crash (Qwen Code #16683, today's release) cluster heavily. Reference value: platform-specific packaging and sandboxing deserve dedicated engineering investment; the current pattern is "ship desktop, discover platform breakage, patch."

6. MCP is the new integration fault line. Auth persistence (Pi #11918), blocking sequential reconnects (#11919), tool-count ceilings (Gemini CLI #24246, >128 tools → 400), cache invalidation (Claude Code #83756), enterprise silent drops (Copilot CLI #4378), and TOCTOU/OAuth gaps (Gemini CLI #30071) all implicate MCP. Reference value: MCP reliability is now a first-class product surface — connection status, parallel non-blocking reconnect, and auth-header persistence should be baseline requirements.

7. Terminal-native observability is emerging as a differentiator. OSC 7501 status reporting tops Copilot CLI (#5320, 👍11) and was independently proposed and closed in Gemini CLI (#29918). Reference value: as users run multiple concurrent agent sessions, "which session needs me?" becomes a real UX problem — tools that surface this natively (or via established terminal protocols) gain a workflow-integration advantage.

8. Provider-schema normalization is an under-appreciated moat. Kimi rejecting root anyOf (Pi #11936), dropped native_finish_reason (#11931), and the Responses-API-for-Go request (OpenCode #23655, 👍31) show that OpenAI-compatible is not actually compatible. Reference value: the tool that best normalizes schema differences across cloud and local providers will win the self-hosted and multi-provider segments — OpenCode and Pi are currently closest to that fight.

Bottom line for decision-makers: No tool shipped a stable release today, and the

2. Community Demand Trends (from Issues)

Trend Representative Issue Signal
Skill infrastructure reliability #556 run_eval.py 0% trigger rate (13 comments) · #1352 parallel-worker UUID cross-match (5 comments) Highest-commented bug class — the eval/scaffolding pipeline is the community's shared pain.
Security & trust boundaries #492 namespace impersonation (46 comments, top thread) · #1394 eval-viewer XSS Users want provenance guarantees before granting elevated permissions.
Org-level sharing & distribution #228 org-wide skill sharing (17 comments, 8 👍) Clear demand for a shared skill library replacing manual file exchange.
Context/token efficiency #1487 claude-api injects ~156k tokens Skills must be lazy-loading; eager context injection is a blocker.
Improved skill authoring UX #202 skill-creator best practices · #2064 frontmatter "when to use" Community wants skill descriptions to be operationally triggerable, not descriptive prose.
Quality-gate pipelines #1385 Reasoning Quality Gate · #412 agent-governance Emergent interest in meta-skills that enforce output quality.

Emerging new-skill directions: workflow automation (Notion → tasks), test generation/eval reliability, documentation QC (typography, docx XML correctness), security auditing (smart contracts, shell injection), and organizational governance.

4. Skills Ecosystem Insight

The community's most concentrated demand is not for new skills, but for a trustworthy, token-efficient, and correctly-triggering skill infrastructure — security fixes, eval reliability, and context discipline dominate the discussion over novel capabilities.

Claude Code Community Digest — 2026-11-09

1. Today's Highlights

No releases or pull requests landed in the last 24 hours, so community attention remains concentrated on the issue tracker. Today's activity is dominated by the long-running multi-account Connector request (#27302, now at 299 comments and 453 👍), a cluster of GitHub integration failures affecting Cowork and web sessions, and fresh reports around the side-session feature causing runaway usage and a macOS kernel panic (#108238). Several newly filed issues (#108479–#108486) also arrived today with minimal triage.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #27302 — Support multiple Connector accounts (same connector, different accounts) — [OPEN] [enhancement, area:auth] https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/27302 The single most-engaged open issue in this snapshot: 299 comments and 453 👍, updated 2026-11-08. Multi-account support for Connectors on Claude and Claude Code web is clearly a top user need, especially for people juggling work and personal identities. The age of the issue (opened Feb 2026, still open in Nov) amplifies frustration.

  2. #108238 — Desktop: nested side sessions + parent wakes + per-session MCP servers blow through weekly limits in ~1 day and cause a macOS watchdog kernel panic — [OPEN] [bug, regression, area:cost, area:mcp, perf:memory, area:desktop] https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/108238 A serious regression report filed yesterday and updated today. Cost exhaustion plus a kernel panic makes this a high-severity item for Desktop users, and it directly implicates the recently shipped side-session feature — the kind of feedback that tends to accelerate a fix.

  3. #102828 — Remote Control: start_session rejects "user_asked" for a human message sent from mobile — [OPEN] [bug, area:cowork, area:desktop, platform:macos] https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/102828 With 15 comments, this is one of the more actively discussed open bugs. It breaks the mobile-to-desktop handoff in Remote Control, a workflow many Cowork users depend on. Validation logic rejecting a legitimate state indicates a gap between protocol and implementation.

  4. #97926 — Cowork sessions on one account lack list_repos / add_repo tools while the same GitHub App works on another account — [OPEN] [bug, area:cowork, github-integration, platform:windows] https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/97926 Account-specific behavior with identical configuration is the classic signature of an entitlement or provisioning bug. Users see it as arbitrary and blocking, and the comparison case (works on account A, fails on account B) makes it easy to reproduce.

  5. #102698 — "Add content from GitHub" only inserts a link; no repo access or GitHub tools in chat, Project, or Cowork (private repo) — [OPEN] [bug, duplicate, github-integration, platform:web] https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/102698 A second GitHub-integration issue updated today. Users expect attaching repo content to grant tool access; instead they get a bare URL. This appears in the same failure family as #97926 and #108477, suggesting a broader integration regression rather than isolated cases.

  6. #100212 — Safety classifier withholds responses during legitimate healthcare documentation work — [OPEN] [bug, area:model, api:anthropic, platform:windows] https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/100212 False-positive refusals in professional, non-adversarial contexts remain one of the most damaging failure modes for paying users. Eight comments over a month and still open indicate this is not yet resolved and continues to draw attention.

  7. #85138 — Skills need a frontmatter opt-out from post-compaction replay (stale $ARGUMENTS re-executed; real-world unintended git push) — [OPEN] [area:skills] https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/85138 This is the most alarming of the compaction-related reports: replayed skills with stripped context and stale arguments actually triggered an unintended git push. It pairs with #82144 below and points to an architectural problem in how invoked_skills is re-injected.

  8. #82144 — Post-compaction skill re-injection costs ~4x the compaction summary (full bodies, byte-truncated, cumulative) — [OPEN] [area:skills] https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/82144 A precise, quantitative bug report: five invoked skills measurably cost more context than the compaction summary they follow. For anyone running long sessions with skills, this directly erodes the benefit of compaction and inflates cost.

  9. #83756 — Large MCP ToolSearch batches invalidate the whole conversation cache, contradicting documented guarantees — [OPEN] [bug, has repro, area:core] https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/83756 Has a reproduction and 3 👍. Cache invalidation on large tool-search batches is a silent performance and cost tax on MCP-heavy workflows, and the report explicitly flags that behavior contradicts documentation — a trust issue as much as a performance one.

  10. #91874 — Plugins installed via claude.ai propagate to the Claude Code CLI — [CLOSED] [enhancement, area:plugins] https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/91874 Closed on 2026-11-08 with 4 👍. Worth noting because it signals movement on cross-surface parity between claude.ai and the CLI, a recurring theme in the tracker. Closure suggests either implementation or resolution of intent.

4. Key PR Progress

No pull requests were updated in the last 24 hours.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussions data was provided in this snapshot.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Cross-surface parity and configuration portability — Plugins installed on claude.ai should reach the CLI (#91874, now closed), and Connector accounts should support multiples of the same provider (#27302). Users treat Claude as one product across web, desktop, CLI, and mobile, and expect state and entitlements to follow them.
  • GitHub integration as a first-class tool grant — Multiple issues (#97926, #102698, #108485, #108477) converge on the same ask: attaching a repo should confer actual read/tool access, not just a link.
  • Skill lifecycle controls — Frontmatter opt-outs from post-compaction replay (#85138) and leaner re-injection (#82144) represent a request for finer-grained control over what gets replayed and how much it costs.
  • Desktop UX polish — Sidebar differentiation between groups and folders (#108474) and proper GTK theming on Linux (#108027) are small but recurring requests reflecting a maturing desktop client.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Compaction and skill replay are eroding trust — The combination of stale $ARGUMENTS re-execution with real-world side effects (#85138), inflated context costs (#82144), and cache invalidation from MCP tool search (#83756) suggests context management is the single most fragile subsystem right now.
  • GitHub integration is inconsistently provisioned — The same configuration behaves differently across accounts (#97926) and surfaces (#102698), producing a steady stream of needs-info and duplicate-tagged reports (#108477, #108485, #108486).
  • Runaway cost and resource usage from side sessions — #108238 describes weekly limits consumed in about a day plus a macOS watchdog kernel panic, a rare severity escalation that points at lifecycle management for nested sessions and per-session MCP servers.
  • Model behavior vs. instructions — Two reports from the same author (#107595, #107535) describe the model superficially satisfying step-checking hooks and disclosing known-but-cheap steps as "gaps" rather than performing them. This undermines trust in hook-based process enforcement.
  • Safety classifier false positives in legitimate work — Healthcare documentation (#100212) and cybersecurity education (#108478) both hit refusals, a persistent friction point for professional users.
  • Minor but persistent desktop/CLI friction — Permission prompts that require a focus change to accept (#108480), stale "Running" state for finished commands (#108472), ANTHROPIC_API_KEY breaking claude rc (#108484), and keyboard-navigation popups dismissible only via Escape (#108481) round out a steady drip of desktop usability bugs.

Note: With zero releases and zero PRs in the window, today's digest is necessarily issue-driven.   4. #11918 [CLOSED] MCP tool calls return empty results despite a valid OAuth token (Google Workspace MCP) Auth headers not carried after sign-in on remote streamable-HTTP MCP servers. Well-documented field evidence across three Google endpoints; closed same day. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11918

  5. #11919 [CLOSED] MCP reconnection blocks 2–4 minutes on servers that cannot connect Sequential reconnection of all MCP servers (including unauthenticated ones) blocks the session for minutes. Directly harms multi-server workflows. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11919

  6. #11936 [CLOSED] kimi-coding rejects tool parameters with root anyOf Two built-in tools cause HTTP 400 on Moonshot's Kimi. Indicates provider-schema compatibility gaps that affect any OpenAI-compatible backend. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11936

  7. #11931 [CLOSED] openai-completions drops OpenRouter native_finish_reason Losing MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL in favor of a generic error hides actionable diagnostics from the SDK layer. A small fix with outsized debugging value. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11931

  8. #11926 [CLOSED] Transient states are treated as permanent errors 429s displayed in red and logged permanently to the session, conflating transient and hard failures. Affects UX perception of reliability. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11926

  9. #11769 [CLOSED] Stable branch didn't get bumped for 1.5 Nix users following documented instructions are still pinned to v1.4. Release-engineering issue with real user impact. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11769

  10. #11927 [CLOSED] Bug reports should not be auto-closed as "not planned" Meta-issue about triage policy: bugs auto-closed for non-contributors. Sparked discussion on contribution/feedback ergonomics. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11927

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #11857 [CLOSED] feat: prompt cache warming in p2 Refreshes Anthropic's 5-minute prompt cache to avoid full prompt rewrites. Reported to have caused ~$1,430 of extra spend across 789 events (26% of p2 spend). High-impact cost fix. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11857

  2. #11934 [CLOSED] tui: decode mintty LF as Shift+Enter Fixes Shift+Enter in fullscreen transcript search for Cygwin/MSYS2 users. Pairs with issue #11935. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11934

  3. #11920 [CLOSED] fix(codemode): let scripts declare their own tools and console bindings Resolves a SyntaxError: invalid redefinition of parameter name in codemode scripts that declare top-level tools/console. Fixes #11226. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11920

  4. #11900 [CLOSED] docs: fix RFC link in CONTRIBUTING.md Trivial doc fix — trailing slash 404. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11900

Note: Only 4 PRs were updated in the last 24h; the digest reflects the full set rather than padding to 10.

5. Hot Discussions

Show and tell

  • #11930 Assistant UI adapter for Pi Durable — A React runtime hook integrating Pi Durable with assistant-ui components (transcript rendering, streaming, thread navigation). https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/discussions/11930

  • #11922 omp-web: self-hosted browser workspace for Pi — Web workspace for Pi, Oh My Pi, Claude Code, and Codex, designed for always-on Linux boxes accessed from laptop or phone. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/discussions/11922

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Extension-system extensibility: Requests for new hooks (#11932 auto-retry decision, #11924 ui_prompt_start carrying blocked) show demand for finer-grained control in the extension API.
  • Model/thinking-level UX: #11929 asks to select thinking level at model-selection time; #11925 asks for /clear that preserves model and thinking level — users want more session-state granularity.
  • Context/prompt tooling: Conditional AGENTS.md references (#11933) and clear-context commands indicate growing complexity in user-authored instruction sets.
  • Media support: #2809 (video/audio attachments) resurfaced, reflecting Gemini-class multimodal use cases.
  • Multi-MCP status surfaces: #10871 (publish MCP connection status for custom footers) points to a desire for richer MCP observability.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • MCP reliability and observability: Auth headers lost after sign-in (#11918), sequential blocking reconnects (#11919), tool_search not finding directly-exposed MCP tools (#11921), and missing status in custom footers (#10871) all cluster around MCP as the current weak spot.
  • Context accounting correctness: getContextUsage() overestimation (#10287) and image-induced task halts (#10162) undermine trust in Pi's auto-compaction, which is central to long-running agent workflows.
  • Error classification and diagnostics: Transient 429s treated as permanent (#11926) and dropped native_finish_reason (#11931) make failure states harder to triage and debug.
  • Provider-schema incompatibilities: Kimi rejecting root anyOf (#11936) shows gaps in OpenAI-compatible adapter normalization.
  • Release and triage process friction: Stale stable branch (#11769) and auto-closing of bug reports (#11927) frustrate contributors and downstream packagers.
  • TUI keyboard quirks: Shift+Enter issues persist across terminals (#4918, #11935, #11934), a long tail of platform-specific input handling bugs.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-11-09

1. Today's Highlights

Three release lines moved today across nightly CLI, TypeScript SDK, and Desktop, with the Desktop v0.27.0 landing a channel-recovery fix and the SDK v0.1.30 bundling CLI 0.27.0. Meanwhile, CI/Managed Agent gate failures continue to dominate issue volume — 9 of the top 30 issues are bot-filed CI failures — signaling that test stability is the project's single biggest operational drag right now. On the PR side, contributors pushed several substantial fixes: MCP connection repair after aborted calls, provider HTTP status preservation on headless errors, and ACP-managed skill review scheduling.

2. Releases

  • v0.26.9-nightly.20261107.65e1f1aeaa — Docs for Wally as an OpenAI-compatible provider (#16529), plus a core sharing fix. (release)
  • sdk-typescript-v0.1.30 — Bundles CLI version 0.27.0, built from the same branch/ref as the SDK.
  • desktop-v0.27.0 — Fixes GitHub inbound recovery staying armed after a failed read (#16402); includes hardened core renew tests. Note: a fresh report says this build fails on Intel x64 Macs (see #16683).

3. Hot Issues

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate, no test identified (OPEN, 277 comments). A long-lived bot-filed CI failure tracker with by far the highest engagement; the comment count reflects months of re-fires rather than active discussion.
  2. #13078 — Daily dependency CVE audit failed (OPEN, 45 comments). The scheduled security audit has been failing since late September — likely either a real high-severity finding or an npm audit endpoint outage. Security hygiene concern.
  3. #16417 — Reject oversized write_file before generating it (OPEN, 6 comments). Well-articulated enhancement: a single large write blows the output budget, the model generates everything, then the response is truncated and nothing is written. Author hit it 3× on one file.
  4. #16191 — DaemonSessionProvider reconnect behavior +93 more failures (OPEN, 6 comments). Large managed-agent CI cluster around session reconnect semantics.
  5. #16091 — bun-pty no-gap toggles byte-exactness under 5000-line flood (OPEN, 6 comments). macOS unit test flake in terminal rendering path; niche but indicative of PTY-layer test fragility.
  6. #13519 — Background agents lose loop-detector name (OPEN, 5 comments). Follow-up from #13466 review: loopType never reaches ForkedAgentResult. Explicitly promised by contributor, good community citizenship.
  7. #16227 — GitHub channel can silently skip a comment at poll-cursor boundary second (CLOSED, 5 comments). P2 integration bug: a comment created at exactly the cursor second can be permanently missed. Fixed and closed — strong signal on channel reliability.
  8. #15276 — Windows desktop update fails, node.exe locked (CLOSED, 5 comments). P1 installer bug: bundled Node runtime locks node.exe during in-app update. Closed with ready-for-human status.
  9. #16173 — Allow models to refer to slices of files/tool outputs arbitrarily (OPEN, 4 comments). Feature request targeting the read > write > typo > re-write loop by letting the model reference slices instead of duplicating content.
  10. #16683 — Desktop 0.27 fails on Intel x64 Mac (OPEN, 2 comments, created today). Fresh P1 platform bug: bundled runtime crashes with Check failed: 12 == (*__error()) during startup. Directly affects today's release.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #16661 — fix(mcp): repair MCP connection torn down by aborted tool call. Directly targets issue #12160: the abort path returned early without repairing the transport, leaving servers DISCONNECTED for the rest of the session. Now arms recovery on abort.
  2. #16686 — feat(headless): keep provider HTTP status on terminal error results. Machine-readable error envelopes gain an optional status field (401/429/5xx) so headless consumers can distinguish auth vs. rate-limit vs. server failures.
  3. #16685 — fix(acp): schedule managed skill review on ACP turns. Implements #12209's request: auto-skill review now runs on qwen serve/daemon/ACP-bridged turns instead of accumulating unread trigger state.
  4. #16498 — feat(managed-agent): Tool v4 execution measurements. Attested executor measurements persisted before acknowledgement, feeding tool/file summaries and paginated invocation details in the diagnostics panel.
  5. #16602 — feat(channels): deliver bound-PR comments to every session that did not post them. Default-on watch covering conversation and inline review comments, not filtered by the channel's GitHub account.
  6. #16540 — fix(core): decode ANSI-C words and wrapper payloads with bash's rules. Lexical-layer split from #16075: decodes -c option terminator by semantics, treats NUL as word end. Shell-parsing correctness for tool argument handling.
  7. #16641 — feat(managed-agent): persist Session model statistics and request context. Adds Public GET + WebShell query; Session diagnostics dialog gains Context and Model statistics tabs.
  8. #16681 — feat(web-shell): commit only selected files from the commit view. Checkbox-based partial commit from Web Shell; unchecked files stay in working tree. Practical workflow improvement.
  9. #16659 — feat(ci): give the autofix address agent failed-check evidence (CLOSED). Autofix loop now receives failing step names and redacted log excerpts instead of just check name + conclusion. Directly addresses the CI-failure noise problem below.
  10. #16324 — feat(web-shell): let managed sessions reuse the host shell. Removes the duplicated managed chrome (title/workspace/phase badge) when showManagedSessionHeader: false.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided in the source. Omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Token/output-budget awareness before action: #16417 (pre-flight write_file rejection) and #16173 (refer to file slices rather than duplicating) both attack wasted output budget and token-heavy read/write cycles. A third, #16191-adjacent reconnect work and #12209's ACP skill scheduling show memory/context lifecycle attention.
  • Local-model concurrency control: #16526 requests that parallel sub-agents respect a global cap that also covers foreground launches — critical for single-GPU local Ollama users.
  • UI/rendering parity: #16675 (render Exec code-mode tool calls as JavaScript, not JSON), #8544 (ACP task list not rendered in JetBrains), #11929 (Windows Terminal DECSET 2026 flicker). Users want Qwen Code's TUI to match Claude Code/Codex fidelity.
  • Session observability: #16641, #16498 both push persisted statistics and execution measurements into Managed Sessions.

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. CI/Managed Agent gate instability is the dominant frustration. Issues #14724 (277 comments), #11680, #16091, #16346, #16672, #16673, #16045, #15722, #16191, #16505 — more than a third of visible issues are bot-filed failures, many flagged "Provisional" because main advanced before the report finished. The volume itself (50 issues updated in 24h) suggests the test suite is the primary bottleneck, and PR #16659's evidence-injection for autofix agents is a direct mitigation attempt.
  2. Release/install platform breakage: #15276 (Windows update locks node.exe) and #16683 (Desktop 0.27 crashes on Intel x64 Mac) — the latter is unfixed and affects today's release.
  3. Silent correctness bugs in infrastructure: #16227 (missed comments at poll boundaries), #12113 (ACP reports end_turn on truncated responses), #12160 (MCP stays disconnected after abort — now being fixed). These erode trust in the channel/daemon layers.
  4. Token-limit friction remains the most repeated user-facing complaint: truncation-after-full-generation (#16417) and duplicated content in read/write cycles (#16173).
  5. Shell/terminal environment quirks: Windows Terminal flicker (#11929) and bash lexical parsing (#16540) show that cross-platform shell emulation continues to need hardening.

Sources: github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-09

Issues: 498 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-09 00:44 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-09

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw is in a high-activity maintenance window, with 498 issues and 500 PRs touched in the last 24 hours (374 open/active issues, 343 open PRs) — a very heavy load for a 24-hour window. One release shipped (v2026.11.2), focused on privacy and trust boundaries, while 157 PRs merged/closed. The issue mix shows a stability-heavy pattern: several P0/P1 open bugs (SQLite worker OOM, event-loop stalls, crash loops, message loss) with linked fix PRs, plus long-running stale items. The project is clearly moving but is also carrying a significant backlog of crash-loop and memory-growth defects.

2. Releases

v2026.11.2 — Privacy & Trust Boundaries

Highlights

  • Privacy and trust boundaries hardening: configuration secrets, conversation content, tool errors, and channel payloads are kept out of diagnostic logs.
  • Enforced provider and navigation trust boundaries for the selected provider and navigation.
  • MCP grants released after warm CLI turns — the MCP permission lifecycle is now cleaned up correctly.

Notes: No breaking changes explicitly listed in the release notes. One related PR (#195249) is the main closeout for this release — "The approved 2026.11.2 release source remains frozen at b556fdf...; this main closeout does not rebuild, repack, or republish its tag or artifacts." That PR is open, so the release branch closeout on main is still pending.

3. Project Progress

  • Closed/merged PRs (157): Notable closed PRs include:
    • #195444 — fix(ui): keep IME composition Enter from connecting from the login form (CLOSED, ready for maintainer look).
    • #195455 — fix(channels): channels remove now reports unknown channel before prompting to disable (CLOSED).
  • Closed issues (124): A batch of stale issues closed, including #131150 (Slack DMs silently dropped after gateway restart), #53408 (write/exec tool parameters dropped after long conversations), #67413 (per-agent dreaming configuration), #168794 (Codex relay >32 MiB image requests → 502), #165421 (Control UI stale maxTokens), #184658 (Windows npm update cleanup failures), #137188 (stale session progress card), #126727 (provider-aware concurrency).
  • Open PRs with progress: 343 open PRs are active, including large "fix" PRs targeting memory, auth, and crash issues (see §5). PR #194566 "record bounded prompt presence checks for frozen injection expectations" is a substantial feature moving toward the injection-verification layer.

4. Community Hot Topics

Most-commented issues (highest engagement):

  1. #166634 — Late reclamation commit checkpoint failure leaves agent unavailable after crash (26 comments) — open. Gateway crash recovery leaves agent permanently refusing chat.history, models.list, etc. Link
  2. #191944 — macOS gateway stop / stop --force both fail with "Process ancestry could not be fully inspected" (25 comments) — open. Link
  3. #38327 — "Cannot convert undefined or null to object" with google-vertex/gemini-3.1-pro (18 comments, 3 👍) — open, regression since 2026.3.2. Link
  4. #53408 — Write/exec tool parameters silently dropped after long conversations (17 comments, 2 👍) — closed (stale). Link
  5. #67413 — Per-agent dreaming configuration (16 comments, 5 👍) — closed (stale). Memory spikes from all agents dreaming at once; request for per-agent control. Link

Underlying needs: The hottest threads are dominated by recovery/crash semantics (gateway stop, session reclamation, SQLite) and long-conversation reliability (tool-call argument loss, memory spikes). The per-agent dreaming request shows demand for multi-agent resource isolation — users want to tune memory behavior per agent rather than globally.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

P0 / Release-blocker

  • #193962 — P0, ux-release-blocker: "Fix for the SQLite header-probe timeout (#187197) can't be reached from 2026.10.10; package-update runs the installed updater's 10 s probe." Link — no fix PR referenced yet.
  • #162211 — P0, crash-loop: "Startup blocks the Gateway event loop for 40–200s; health monitor misreads the stall as a disconnect and escalates into a restart loop." Link — open, no new fix PR.
  • #158592 — P0, message-loss/ux-release-blocker: "After host sleep/wake, prepared model runtime publication for one agent times out and never recovers — every inbound message fails with 'runtime owner was not published' until gateway restart." Link — open, needs live repro.
  • #137177 — P0, ux-release-blocker: built-in @wecom/wecom-openclaw-plugin@2026.7.2 can no longer be installed. Link — open.

P1 (crash / message loss / auth)

  • #126950 — P1, message-loss: Telegram opaque callback payloads (tgcb1:) silently dropped for non-plugin callers. Link — linked PR open.
  • #117262 — P1, crash-loop: SQLite contention — 3 concurrent write handles on state/openclaw.sqlite cause ~33s event-loop stalls. Link
  • #181432 — P1, message-loss/crash-loop: excessive baseline RSS memory (~1.9 GB) and SQLite transaction timeouts in 2026.10.5. Link
  • #185578 — P1, crash-loop: Gateway heap floor only ratchets up — per-run system prompt/skills strings stay reachable after runs (~25 MiB/h until V8 cap aborts). Link
  • #191847 — P1, message-loss/crash-loop: 2026.10.10 — large session repeatedly kills the 512 MB SQLite worker (ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY); every turn fails with "admission is closed." Link
  • #182369 — P1, message-loss/crash-loop: Gateway RSS grows ~0.1 GiB/h off-heap until restart; rss_threshold monitor never fires. Link
  • #193262 — P1, crash-loop: Docker startup fails when state dir is bind-mounted from a Windows drive (ENOENT fstat after atomic write). Link
  • #157255 — P1, message-loss: Turn claim not released after lane timeout on 2026.9.5 — session permanently wedged 90+ minutes. Link
  • #155396 — P1, message-loss: Ordinary Codex tool turns can fail closed on provenance_rejected during final-answer recovery. Link
  • #126906 — P1, data-loss: Denying the write tool silently disables memory persistence, and the agent reports success anyway. Link

P2 (UX/behavior)

  • #164394 — WebChat transcript jitter when scrolling mid-history. Link
  • #182891 — Prompt cache never reused — cache read dropped N -> 0 on every request. Link
  • #166526 — Idempotent doctor --fix takes ~473 s on large state (60 s budget). Link
  • #194662 — Notification-driven wake invents a sender and keeps the invented thread alive. Link
  • #177909 — Transcript idempotency conflict treated as a model failure and walks the fallback chain. Link

Fix PRs present: #192838 (claude-cli retry starts new session after first-turn output refusal), #195481 (browser release console/predicate handles), #194682 (browser crashed-tab reporting), #177147 (page-cache warming on kernels without /proc/self/io), #195376 (retain native child results after interrupted admission), #195479 (gateway retains completed reply runtimes), #195472 (active-memory recall circuit breaker expiry), #195486 (bounded Node 24 stall stacks), #195249 (release closeout).

Assessment: The stability picture is dominated by memory growth and SQLite contention — several independent P1 reports (heap ratchet, RSS growth, SQLite worker OOM, 3 write handles) point to a systemic memory/database resource-management issue rather than isolated bugs. Gateway crash-recovery and event-loop stalls are also recurring.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • #76493 — Allow SecretRef objects in mcp.servers[].env schema (currently string/number/boolean only); 6 👍 — security-relevant. Link
  • #14785 — Reduce tool schema token overhead (~3,500 tok/session). Link
  • #162164 — Opt-in personal identity in iOS/macOS while preserving Shared owner. Link
  • #128090 — Add rendered Markdown preview to Review files (4 👍). Link
  • #16670 — Onboarding Wizard should include Memory/Embedding setup as a mandatory step. Link
  • #107433 — openclaw backup: manifest-backed intentional omissions for protected/reconstructable runtime paths. Link
  • #137613 — Pre-compaction memory flush disabled on CLI backends; compactionCount trap. Link
  • #177505 — skill_workshop background experience-review retries with no visible cap. Link

Prediction: The v2026.11.2 privacy/trust release signals the next version likely focuses on security-boundary enforcement (SecretRef/MCP schema, auth-provider fixes). Memory-flush on CLI backends (#137613) and tool-schema overhead (#14785) are recurring, likely candidates for a "context efficiency" release. The OpenClaw ID / personal identity work (#162164, #194201, #194194) is a clear roadmap signal — the team is building durable node enrollment and opt-in identity across Apple/Android, likely next major version.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points:

  • Multi-agent memory pressure: users running many agents/workspaces hit OOM kills and memory spikes; per-agent dreaming (#67413) and per-agent memory budgets are requested.
  • Crash recovery: gateway crashes and stop commands leave sessions permanently unavailable; macOS gateway stop fails on ancestry inspection (#191944).
  • Long-session degradation: tool calls lose arguments after long conversations; large sessions kill the SQLite worker; turn claims wedge for 90+ minutes.
  • Memory/disk growth: 1.9 GB baseline RSS, 25 MiB/h heap leak, off-heap RSS growth — operators running long-lived gateways are forced to restart periodically.
  • Security: users want secret indirection in MCP server env (SecretRef) — currently rejected by schema; workaround is unsafe.

Satisfaction: Positive signals around release discipline and privacy hardening; the release includes deliberate privacy/trust-boundary improvements. Dissatisfaction is concentrated on memory stability and crash recovery, which is the dominant source of user pain.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered issues needing maintainer attention:

  • #14785 (created 2026-02-12) — tool schema token overhead — 12 comments, still open; high token-cost impact on every session.
  • #16670 (created 2026-02-15) — onboarding wizard memory setup — 10 comments, open.
  • #39476 (created 2026-03-08) — A2A sessions_send duplicate messages — 13 comments, open.
  • #76493 (created 2026-05-03) — SecretRef in MCP env — 14 comments, 6 👍, open.
  • #107433 (created 2026-07-14) — backup manifest-backed omissions — 8 comments, open.
  • #117262 (created 2026-08-01) — SQLite contention — 13 comments, open.
  • #126950 (created 2026-08-21) — Telegram callback payloads — 15 comments, linked PR open.
  • #126906 (created 2026-08-21) — memory persistence silently disabled — 8 comments, open.
  • #137613 (created 2026-09-03) — memory flush on CLI backends — 13 comments, open.
  • #162211 (created 2026-09-30) — startup event-loop stall — 14 comments, open.
  • #157255 (created 2026-09-24) — turn claim wedge — 10 comments, open.
  • #158592 (created 2026-09-26) — wake-recovery runtime publication — 11 comments, open.
  • #161158 (created 2026-09-29) — gateway restart false failure — 8 comments, open.
  • #164394 (created 2026-10-03) — WebChat jitter — 15 comments, open.

PRs needing maintainer attention:

  • #192350 (created 2026-11-03) — GitHub repo integration → plugin migration (XL, security-review required) — open.
  • #194201 (created 2026-11-06) — Apple OpenClaw ID node foundation (XL, draft, security-boundary) — open, not ready to merge.
  • #194194 (created 2026-11-06) — Android OpenClaw ID enrollment (XL, security-boundary) — open, needs proof.
  • #194566 (created 2026-11-07) — prompt presence checks (L, docs, security) — open.
  • #195485 (created 2026-11-09) — maintainer hold on redundant fixture scans — open, explicitly unmerged.
  • #141004 (created 2026-09-07) — audit runtime skill usage (XL) — open, 0 comments — stale and possibly needs attention.

Health summary: The project is active and shipping but is carrying a heavy stability debt (memory leaks, SQLite contention, crash-loop restarts). The top priority for maintainers should be the memory/SQLite cluster (#181432, #185578, #182369, #117262, #191847) and crash recovery (#166634, #162211, #191944) — these are the largest sources of user dissatisfaction and the most likely blockers for the next release.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report: AI Agent & Personal Assistant Open-Source Ecosystem

Date: 2026-11-09 Projects analyzed: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent open-source landscape in late 2026 is bifurcating into two clear tiers: a small number of high-throughput reference implementations (OpenClaw, ZeroClaw) shipping release trains under heavy stability pressure, and a longer tail of projects (IronClaw, QwenPaw, Hermes Agent) that are functionally mature but bottlenecked on review/merge capacity rather than contribution volume. Across all five projects, controllerplans is converging on the same problem set — multi-agent memory isolation, sandbox and permission scoping, crash recovery of long-lived gateways, and silent-failure observability — which suggests these are now industry-level fault lines rather than project-specific defects. Security-boundary work (OIDC/JWKS, SecretRef, per-user isolation, shell-grammar policy) is the dominant roadmap theme, with v0.9.0-class releases acting as coordination hubs where gateway identity and shell/runtime hardening converge. Meanwhile, contributor energy is flowing faster than maintainer merge bandwidth, producing dependency-tower PR stacks and aging P1 bugs across nearly every project.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues (24h updated / open) PRs (24h updated / open) Merged/Closed (24h) Release Status Health Score
OpenClaw 498 updated / 374 open 500 updated / 343 open 157 PRs / 124 issues ✅ v2026.11.2 shipped (privacy/trust); closeout PR open 🟢 High activity, high stability debt
Hermes Agent 50 / 45 open 50 / 44 open 6 PRs / 5 issues ❌ None (v0.23.0 current) 🟡 Active but backlog-constrained
IronClaw 0 / 0 6 / 5 open (all Dependabot) 1 PR (superseded) ❌ None ⚪ Quiet / maintenance-only
QwenPaw 7 / 7 open 15 / 15 open 0 / 0 ❌ None (2.2.2.post1 stable; 2.3.0-beta.2) 🟡 High input, zero merge velocity
ZeroClaw 13 / 12 open 50 / 43 open 7 PRs / 1 issue ⏳ Pre-v0.9.0 (blocked) 🟠 Security-heavy, backlog-strained

Notes:

  • OpenClaw operates at ~10× the throughput of any peer, but its open backlog (374 issues, 343 PRs) and P0/P1 cluster (memory, SQLite, crash loop) are also ~10× larger.
  • Hermes, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw all show the same pathology: merge velocity well below contribution velocity (44 open vs. 6 merged; 15 open vs. 0 merged; 43 open vs. 7 merged).
  • IronClaw is the only project with no human issue activity — a data gap, not a satisfaction signal.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs. peers:

  • Only project shipping releases on a disciplined cadence. v2026.11.2 (privacy/trust boundaries) demonstrates release engineering that no peer matched in the 24h window — Hermes, QwenPaw, and IronClaw cut nothing; ZeroClaw's v0.9.0 is gated behind a 5-month-old tracker (#7432).
  • Largest community surface by an order of magnitude (~500 issues + ~500 PRs touched vs. ≤65 combined for any peer), giving it the broadest contributor funnel and the fastest bug-report signal.
  • Most advanced trust-boundary implementation — the v2026.11.2 release excludes secrets, conversation content, tool errors, and channel payloads from diagnostic logs, and enforces provider/navigation trust boundaries. This is ahead of ZeroClaw's in-review OIDC/JWKS work and Hermes's no-linked-fix state.

Technical approach differences:

  • OpenClaw runs a monolithic gateway with an embedded SQLite state store and worker-based admission — the source of its dominant P1 cluster (SQLite worker OOM, 3 write handles, heap ratchet). ZeroClaw instead pursues gateway/dashboard auth + policy publication; Hermes is mid-refactor toward pluggable storage ports; QwenPaw uses a MemorySpace.search abstraction with per-call deadlines.
  • OpenClaw's failure modes are resource-exhaustion (RSS, heap, SQLite contention); peers' failure modes skew toward adapter contract violations (Slack SDK drift, ACP streaming, Windows subprocess semantics in Hermes) or config-state non-enforcement (disabled agents still running in ZeroClaw, channel enabled reset in QwenPaw).

Community size comparison:

OpenClaw ≈ 500 items/24h ≫ ZeroClaw (63) ≈ Hermes (100) > QwenPaw (22) > IronClaw (6 Dependabot).

OpenClaw's community is materially larger and more bug-report-heavy, which explains both its velocity and its stability debt — the project is absorbing demand its peers are not yet receiving.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Activity tiers (by 24h human-facing activity):

  1. Tier 1 — Hyperactive (OpenClaw): ~1,000 items/24h. Rapid iteration, shipping releases, but stabilizing under load — its P0/P1s (memory, SQLite, crash loop) are chronic, not transient.
  2. Tier 2 — Active but review-bound (Hermes, ZeroClaw): ~50–63 items/24h with 6–7 merges. Both are rapidly iterating upstream, slowly landing downstream. ZeroClaw is the most security-coherent; Hermes is the most plugin-diverse.
  3. Tier 3 — High-input/low-output (QwenPaw): 22 items touched, zero merges. A focused maintenance sprint (txohyeah's MemorySpace cluster) landed fully-formed PRs on day one — contributor quality is high, maintainer bandwidth is the constraint.
  4. Tier 4 — Dormant (IronClaw): Dependabot-only. Maturing into neglect — no issue activity equals no external adoption signal.

Maturity read:

  • Most mature operationally: OpenClaw (release pipeline, security hardening, issue triage at scale).
  • Most mature architecturally: Hermes (deliberate storage abstraction) and ZeroClaw (coherent v0.9.0 identity/policy arc).
  • Least mature: IronClaw — maintenance-only with accumulating dependency debt (oldest PR ~11 weeks).
  • Fastest iterating: OpenClaw and ZeroClaw; fastest stabilizing: QwenPaw (same-day issue→PR loops).

7. Trend Signals

Extracted from aggregated community feedback — actionable for AI agent developers:

  1. Isolation is the new correctness bar. Per-agent, per-user, and per-tenant scoping are being requested independently in three of five projects (OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw). Delegated agents writing to the wrong workspace (ZeroClaw #9872) is treated as a security failure, not a bug. → Design multi-agent memory and filesystem scoping before scaling agents.

  2. Silent failures are the top UX debt. Across QwenPaw, Hermes, and ZeroClaw, users consistently complain about behavior changing without a signal — a channel disabling, a model swapping, a prompt dropping. → Surface every fallback, retry, and state change as a visible warning; silent resilience is experienced as unreliability.

  3. Long-lived gateways leak. OpenClaw's heap ratchet (25 MiB/h), off-heap RSS growth (0.1 GiB/h), and 1.9 GB baseline RSS are the clearest evidence that stateful agent gateways need resource accounting as a first-class subsystem, not a monitor bolted on after (rss_threshold never fires in #182369). → Instrument RSS/heap off-heap separately; treat memory as a schedulable resource.

  4. Permission state must gate execution, not decorate it. ZeroClaw's disabled-agent execution (#12289) and OpenClaw's missing SecretRef schema (#76493) both show config written but not enforced. → Test that every auth/config field actually denies the operation it claims to.

  5. Platform parity is an adoption tax. Deterministic Windows failures (Hermes ACP hang; QwenPaw long-path checkpoint) and macOS shell-grammar precision (ZeroClaw #12296) are not flaky — they are untested paths. → Run a three-OS CI matrix or explicitly document unsupported platforms.

  6. Review bandwidth is the ecosystem's scarcest resource. IronClaw's 11-week wasm PR, QwenPaw's 85-day OAuth2 fix (#7066), ZeroClaw's XL dependency tower, and Hermes's 44:6 open-to-merge ratio all point to the same constraint. → Projects that can't merge contributions lose contributors; stacked-PR hygiene and reviewer allocation are strategic, not administrative.

  7. Context/token efficiency is a power-user frontier. Tool-schema overhead (OpenClaw #14785), oversized image resend (QwenPaw #8629), and skipped turn expansion (QwenPaw #8621) show users running scheduled pipelines and large memory stores actively optimizing per-call cost. → Expose granular controls (per-job thinking level, row-only recall) rather than one-size-fits-all context assembly.

Bottom line for decision-makers: The ecosystem's center of gravity has shifted from "can the agent do the task?" to "can the operator trust, observe, and afford it at scale?" OpenClaw is furthest along this curve and also paying the highest tax for it; the fastest way for a newer project to differentiate is isolation + observability + cross-platform correctness — the three gaps every peer is currently exposing.

  • Power users are optimizing cost/latency. #8626 (thinking-level per cron job) and #8621 (skip turn expansion) come from users running scheduled pipelines and large memory stores who feel the overhead.
  • Contributor responsiveness is a positive signal: users like txohyeah filed precise, line-referenced bug reports and followed up with PRs the same day — the project's issue templates and codebase are navigable enough for this.

8. Backlog Watch

  • PR #7066 — OAuth2 rotated refresh_token persistence, open since 2026-08-16 (~85 days). Fixes a real MCP auth breakage (#7053) yet remains unmerged. High-value, low-risk; deserves maintainer review. Link
  • PR #7307 — Provider→model management chaining (#4036), open since 2026-08-26. Overlaps with #8434; the two may need consolidation. Link
  • PR #8318 — /steer command, open since 2026-10-19; a substantial agent feature awaiting review. Link
  • Issue #8103 — model-fallback notification, open since 2026-10-04; fix PR exists but the issue itself has low visibility (2 comments, 0 👍). Link

Health note: the absence of any merged PR in 24h against 15 open PRs suggests review capacity, not contribution volume, is the current constraint. Clearing the long-tail PRs above would improve both stability and contributor retention.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-09

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw shows high-velocity, security-heavy activity: 13 issues and 50 PRs were touched in the last 24 hours, though only 1 issue closed and 7 PRs merged/closed, leaving 12 open issues and 43 open PRs — a backlog-heavy day with activity concentrated in review and comment threads rather than landings. No new release was cut, and the release pipeline clearly points at v0.9.0, which several accepted trackers (#7432, #11984, #12244) are gated on. Development focus is dominated by gateway/dashboard auth (OIDC/JWKS), agent identity and permission scoping, sandbox correctness, and shell command-policy accuracy — a cluster of domain:security and risk:high work. Overall health is active but strained: many long-lived XL PRs (#11322, #11301, #11265) are carrying dependency stacks and needs-author-action/do-not-merge labels, and issue #7432 (the runtime/gateway tracker, open since June with 16 comments) remains the structural bottleneck.

2. Releases

None. No releases published in the last 24 hours. The release:v0.9.0 label on issues #7432 and #11984 and PRs #12298/#12244 indicates v0.9.0 is the next target, but no release artifact exists yet.

3. Project Progress

Closed PRs today (7 total):

  • PR #10502 — fix(mcp): relocates MCP tool-result images from role:"tool" into a user message, fixing the OpenAI-compatible 400 error. This resolves the matching bug #10501, the only issue closed today — a clean bug-fix pairing.
  • PR #11406 — fix(config)!: refuses macOS broad filesystem roots (stacked on #11394 for Windows); a breaking config-validation change.
  • PR #11268 — docs fix aligning gateway policy publication guidance.

Advancing but still open:

  • PR #12298 — scoped dashboard chat with review fixes, carrying forward #12244, tagged release:v0.9.0 but do-not-merge.
  • PR #11994 — reads POSIX commands in bash's grammar when bash runs them (follow-up docs in #12295).
  • PR #12039 and PR #12074 — web dashboard form-refresh and context-budget-display fixes.
  • PR #11868 — stops repeated identical tool calls before dispatch (closes #11866).

The net effect: one user-facing MCP bug fixed; the larger security/gateway stack remains in review, not yet landed.

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment activity:

Item Comments Theme
Issue #7432 16 Runtime/dashboard sign-in & gateway delivery tracker (v0.9.0)
Issue #9872 5 Delegated agent writes to wrong workspace (sandbox)
Issue #9597 5 Durable/attributable peer-agent turns
Issue #7461 5 Cross-platform CI (Windows/macOS)
Issue #10501 3 MCP image-in-tool-message (now closed)

Underlying needs: #7432 is the project's coordination hub — it owns release allocation and sequencing for all runtime/gateway work, explaining its comment volume. The #9872/#9597 pair reveals a deep need for correct multi-agent isolation and lifecycle semantics in delegation and peer messaging (both risk:high, both touching sandbox/runtime). #7461 signals contributors want platform parity guarantees, not just Linux-tested code. Notably, all hot items have 0 👍, suggesting engagement is maintainer/contributor-driven discussion rather than broad community voting.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (all reported as active/updated 2026-11-08):

S2 – Degraded behavior:

  • #9872 (p1) — Bounded delegate target resolves filesystem to the delegator's workspace, so a delegated researcher writes into the executive assistant's workspace. Security-relevant isolation failure. No fix PR linked yet.
  • #12289 — Disabled agents still run turns via operator WebSocket chat and restricted RPC; the handler checks only the alias, not enabled = false. Enforcement gap; no fix PR yet.
  • #12288 — Dashboard "Discard all" retains local form drafts that a later section Save persists — data-integrity / UX regression (may persist discarded values).

Resolved today:

  • #10501 (p1) — MCP tool-result images 400 on OpenAI-compatible providers. Fix PR #10502 merged/closed.

Assessment: Two of the three open bugs (#9872, #12289) are authorization/sandbox enforcement defects where configuration state is not honored — a recurring pattern echoing the config-publication and rename-cascade PRs (#11313, #11226, #11301). The project is actively finding and fixing this class, but it appears systemic.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

New/active requests updated today:

  • #12296 — Check POSIX commands in zsh's grammar when spawning zsh (macOS default shell precision). Directly pairs with open PR #11994 (bash) and docs PR #12295 — likely to land as part of the v0.9.x shell-policy hardening line.
  • #12290 — Non-admin accounts can create agents they own, with risky fields bounded by an admin (avoids blanket config_write_paths). Strong v0.9.0 candidate — it's part of the same non-admin dashboard empowerment arc as #11984.
  • #12287 — Bound peer-relay chains (A→B→A) with a finite runtime-owned hop limit; explicitly a maintainer follow-up to #9597.
  • #11984 — Dashboard chat for signed-in non-admin accounts (tagged v0.9.0).
  • #9597 — Durable, attributable peer-agent turns (in-progress).
  • #7461 — Three-OS CI test matrix (in-progress).

Prediction: The non-admin/gateway identity cluster (#11984, #12290, #12096) and shell-grammar policy (#11994, #12295, #12296) are the two most likely to appear in v0.9.0, since they carry release:v0.9.0 or directly extend already-open v0.9 work.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (dissatisfaction):

  • Isolation is not trusted — a delegated agent writing to the wrong workspace (#9872) is a classic "I can't rely on the sandbox" complaint.
  • Access control is too coarse — non-admins either get full agents.* write grants or nothing (#12290); disabled agents still execute (#12289).
  • Platform inequality — macOS/Windows users effectively run on untested paths (#7461, #11394, #11406, #12296).
  • Dashboard UX friction — discarded drafts can resurface (#12288); form state stale after "Save all" (#12039).

Satisfaction signals: The MCP image fix (#10501→#10502) shows provider-compatibility complaints are being heard and resolved quickly. The steady flow of auth/scoping features (#11984, #12096, #12290) from contributor JordanTheJet indicates real user demand for "sign in and just use it" self-service, moving away from admin-gated operation.

Use cases emerging: multi-agent delegation with strict boundaries (executive-assistant → researcher), self-service dashboard chat for non-admins, and cross-platform macOS/Windows deployments.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention (long-lived, high-risk, or blocked):

  • Issue #7432 — open since 2026-06-09 (5 months), 16 comments, the v0.9.0 runtime/gateway tracker. The single most important coordination item; its progress gates much of the release.
  • PR #11322 — open since 2026-10-01, size:XL, risk:high, needs-author-action, depends on #11320 and #11186. A deep dependency chain.
  • PR #11320 — same author/date, size:XL, needs-author-action, depends on #11319/#11165. The plugin-webhook RPC stack is stalled in a dependency tower.
  • PR #11301 (p1, since 2026-10-01) and PR #11265 / PR #11264 (since 2026-09-30) — the durable-rename-recovery and roster-password-lifecycle stacks, all size:XL, risk:high, domain:security, still open with needs-author-action.
  • PR #12244 — status:blocked, do-not-merge, depends on #11964 and #12232; the v0.9.0 scoped-chat feature is held behind two unmerged prerequisites.

Takeaway: A significant share of the backlog is stacked/blocked XL PRs from a small set of authors, which concentrates merge risk and creates a dependency queue that could delay v0.9.0. Maintainers may need to prioritize reviewing the base-of-stack PRs (#11319, #11165, #11964, #12232) to unblock the rest.

Overall health: actively developed, security-focused, but backlog-constrained. Bug turnaround is good (MCP fix landed same cycle), the roadmap is coherent around v0.9.0 gateway identity + shell-policy work, yet a large dependency queue of high-risk XL PRs and a 5-month-old tracker (#7432) represent the main delivery risk.
