GitHub Copilot CLI — github/copilot-cli

GitHub Copilot CLI Community Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Highlights

Release activity continues at a rapid cadence with v1.0.108-0, which introduces a Windows-specific sandbox enumeratePaths grant and turns on managed shared tgrep indexing by default for eligible repos via new /index commands. Meanwhile, community attention is split between lingering input-handling bugs (Shift+Enter, IME submission) and a cluster of Entra-broker/MCP authentication regressions on both Windows and macOS, plus continued cleanup around the 1.0.106/1.0.107 release-note duplication.

2. Releases

v1.0.108-0 (latest)

  • Added: sandbox.userPolicy.filesystem.enumeratePaths in settings.json for Windows enumerate-only directory grants.
  • Added: /index commands, with managed shared tgrep indexing now enabled by default for eligible repositories.
  • Improved: Answering questions about Copilot CLI behavior from this build.

v1.0.107 (2026-11-06)

  • Rex terminals render inline images using Kitty direct placements.
  • Added /code command to open the current session in VS Code.
  • Added a Fusion tier setting to copilot config.
  • /settings now opens the unified dashboard for all users, with global search across settings and local resources.

v1.0.106 (2026-11-05)

  • Identical notes to v1.0.107 (see Issue #5377 flagging the duplication).

3. Hot Issues

  1. #1972 — Allow users to configure submit key (e.g., Ctrl+Enter) to prevent accidental submission with IME input. 48 👍 and years of CJK-user demand make this the highest-signal input request; Enter currently doubles as IME conversion and prompt submission.
  2. #2776 — Shift+Enter submits instead of inserting a newline. 5 👍, still open since April; companion issue #3768 confirms it reproduces even with multiline terminal enabled.
  3. #5236 — Windows: Entra broker token cache stays 0 bytes after MCP sign-in. Every new process re-prompts for account selection; 1,972-byte cache file writes but is never reused.
  4. #5250 — macOS: Entra-broker MCP servers fail at startup with "sign-in is already in progress." Concurrent sign-ins to Azure DevOps and WorkIQ MCP servers reject each other; rejected cached tokens are not recovered.
  5. #3679 — BYOK Azure OpenAI 429 throttling exhausts all retries in ~0.15s. No backoff, no configurable retry count — high impact for self-hosted/air-gapped deployments.
  6. #5362 — Model-judged context pruning. Proposal lets the model swap junk tool results for a one-line summary, avoiding poisoned context for the rest of the session. Fresh design discussion with strong conceptual merit.
  7. #4150 — permissions-config.json commandIdentifiers with spaces still require approval. "make fix" fails while "make" succeeds, undermining the auto-approve allowlist.
  8. #5367 — Agent regularly loses MCP tool schemas mid-session. Daily-impact bug; users report /compact as the only workaround to restore tool visibility.
  9. #5366 — Remote MCP OAuth (Entra): calls fail after token expiry while mcp.list still reports connected. Only restartServer recovers, a real problem for long-running SDK sessions.
  10. #5370 — Agent output withheld until next user turn when long shell commands are backgrounded (Fusion/Auto mode). Makes the agent appear hung until the user pings it again.

4. Key PR Progress

Only one PR was updated in the window:

  1. #5373 — docs: add Simplified Chinese Copilot CLI README. Adds a translated README plus mutual EN/ZH navigation links, preserving commands, config keys, and product names. Opens the door to broader i18n contribution patterns for the project.

(No other PRs were active in the last 24h; the PR list is otherwise empty.)

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this window, so this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Input ergonomics & IME support — Configurable submit key (#1972), Shift+Enter newline (#2776, #3768), scrollback collapsing/highlighting (#4995). This is the most persistent cluster of asks.
  • Granular permission control — Space-containing commandIdentifiers (#4150), disabling built-in slash commands to avoid skill collisions (#5375), reporting sandbox temp-storage rules (#5365).
  • Model routing & provider control — Block lists for Fusion/Auto mode (#5369), fixing BYOK retry/backoff behavior (#3679), honoring COPILOT_PROVIDERS_CONFIG in --host-environment/--server modes (#5371).
  • Context/memory hygiene — Model-judged context pruning (#5362) and preventing MCP schema loss (#5367).
  • Hooks & extensibility — Display-only hooks for redacted assistant messages (#5099), rendering postToolUse hook output in desktop (#5374).
  • Internationalization — Simplified Chinese README (#5373) reflects a growing non-English contributor/user base.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Authentication reliability for Entra/MCP is the loudest theme: empty token caches on Windows (#5236), concurrent sign-in rejection on macOS (#5250), and silent OAuth token expiry with misleading mcp.list status (#5366). Users are re-authenticating far too often.
  • Input handling regressions continue to frustrate: Shift+Enter submission (#2776, #3768), Esc discarding entire ask_user forms instead of clearing input (#4943), and command history being last-writer-wins across concurrent processes (#5265).
  • Silent or stuck-feeling agent behavior — withheld Fusion/Auto output (#5370) and MCP tool schema disappearance (#5367) erode trust in long-running sessions.
  • Retry/network resilience — near-instant retry exhaustion on Azure OpenAI 429s (#3679) with no user-tunable backoff.
  • Release-note quality — duplicated 1.0.106/1.0.107 notes (#5377) and ambiguous changelog content draw attention away from substantive changes.
  • Platform/Windows sandbox edge cases — the CreateProcessW sandbox probe failure (#5368, now closed) and new enumeratePaths support signal the team is actively hardening Windows isolation.
OpenCode — anomalyco/opencode

OpenCode Community Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Highlights

OpenCode shipped v2.2.6, headlined by shared MCP connection pooling (fewer processes, faster startup) and new GUI plugin theming slots. The community remains heavily focused on free-tier reliability (#59387 has ballooned to 315 comments) and a cluster of V2 regressions around compaction, subagent lifecycle, and TUI model selection. PR activity is concentrated on the Code Mode VM (durable tools, per-namespace catalogs) and config hot-reload fixes for symlinked files.

2. Releases

v2.2.6 — release note

  • Shared MCP Connections: Connection pooling for MCP servers lets projects with identical setups share a single connection — fewer spawned processes, faster cold starts. (#61185)
  • GUI Plugin Themes & New Slots: GUI plugins can now ship themes and hook into additional named slots. (release notes truncated upstream)

3. Hot Issues

  1. #59387 — Free tier megathread (315 comments, 👍23) — Central tracking issue for Free usage exceeded, non-resetting quotas, and Desktop version rejections. This is the single loudest signal in the repo right now; free-tier UX is the top community concern.

  2. #40993 — Support the Agent Plugins standard (👍21) — Request for agent-plugins.org, a vendor-neutral packaging spec bundling Agent Skills + MCP servers. High upvote count suggests multi-vendor portability is a strategic ask, not a niche one.

  3. #27110 — Limit max parallel subagents (👍42) — Highest-upvoted open feature. Local-model users on constrained VRAM need a concurrency cap; today parallel tasks thrash memory.

  4. #51949 — Agent loses top-level tools after auto-compact — Post-compaction the agent silently falls back to code mode, breaks, and reports it has no tools. A serious correctness bug for long sessions.

  5. #48826 — V2 subagent marked completed with pending background work — Parent agents are notified early with premature results; background task output is never collected. Reproduced and still open — matters for anyone orchestrating subagents.

  6. #62442 — Desktop stuck session: interrupt returns false, delete times out (499) — Session can enter an unrecoverable running state on 2.2.5. Fresh but escalating; blocking for Desktop users.

  7. #62447 — TUI model picker shows subset of custom provider models — Only 3 of 7 Ollama models appear despite the server returning all 7. Directly undercuts @ai-sdk/openai-compatible custom provider workflows.

  8. #61507 — TUI discards --model when resuming a session — --agent is honored, --model is not: the resumed session reverts to the last user message's model. Breaks scripted/CI workflows.

  9. #62415 — Agent markdown with name + V2 permissions ignores permissions — Teams porting from Claude Code (which requires name) get silently disabled permission rules. A security-adjacent config trap.

  10. #62432 — No way to disable persisting "Allow always" approvals — One-off clicks silently override ask rules in opencode.json, with inconsistent behavior across projects. Permission-model governance gap.

Also notable: #57844 and #62411 (multilingual glyph corruption in GLM free models), #62138 (/goal stuck after /undo), #40096 (collapsible tool output).

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #62459 — durable tools & safe suspension in Code Mode VM — Adds false | "rerun" | { start, attach, cancel } durability semantics and stable <runId>:<callId> keys. Foundational for reliable long-running VM tooling.

  2. #62176 — per-namespace Code Mode catalog sections — Fixes the shared 2,000-token catalog budget that caused one namespace's change to reshuffle all others (~2,400 tokens restated per update).

  3. #62444 — Code Mode VM enabled by default in dev — Migrates codemode_vm into the flag registry so it resolves like todo/artifacts. Signals VM path is nearing default-on.

  4. #62429 — { url, headers } sources for instructions and skills — Lets OpenCode Console share workspace instructions/skills via remote sources; enables hosted/team config distribution.

  5. #53932 — reload symlinked config targets — Fixes stale opencode.json when the symlink target (e.g. dotfiles repo) is edited outside the watched directory.

  6. #62457 — watch symlinked config file targets — Companion fix covering global config symlinks into dotfiles; changes like model now apply without recreation.

  7. #58846 — repair V1 global sessions from completed imports — Retroactive fix for users already upgraded past #56322 whose V1 sessions were never attributed to project folders.

  8. #61073 — label Claude Agent requests as opencode — Stops Agent SDK requests being mislabeled sdk-ts; improves telemetry attribution for Claude Code bridging.

  9. #62249 — keep grep results on non-UTF-8 matches — Non-UTF-8 files (Latin-1, GBK) no longer abort grep with Invalid ripgrep output; relevant for i18n codebases.

  10. #62423 — accept model prefixes without breaking utility commands — Launchers injecting --model provider/model can now pass through export etc., without disturbing resumed-session model selection.

Also: #62445 (site perf: stats reels restyling, WebKit reload jump), #62458 / #62446 / #62443 (Console model docs: Inkling 2 Small Free added, Pulse Alpha Free deprecated, Iceman Free added), #60957 (nix hashes).

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussions data was provided in this dataset — section omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Resource governance for local models — Cap parallel subagents (#27110, 👍42) so context/memory aren't exhausted; a clear top ask from the local-inference crowd.
  • Ecosystem interoperability — Adopt the vendor-neutral Agent Plugins standard (#40993) to make Skills + MCP bundles portable across agents.
  • TUI ergonomics — Collapsible tool output (#40096) and other noise-reduction controls for long sessions.
  • Platform-native desktop polish — Custom titlebars on Linux/GNOME (#36225) and project deletion in Desktop (#28030, since closed).
  • Permission control granularity — Opt-out of persistent "Allow always" approvals (#62432).
  • Output-language guarding — Deterministic language control for multilingual models (#57844).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Free-tier quota opacity — The dominant pain point. Non-resetting limits, inconsistent Desktop behavior, and error messages without remedy — consolidated into #59387 (315 comments).
  • Compaction correctness — Auto-compaction triggers below threshold (#62218) and, worse, strips top-level tool access afterwards (#51949). Long-session reliability is at risk.
  • Subagent lifecycle bugs — Premature completed status with pending background work (#48826) and stalled multi-step agents (#61511) undermine orchestration trust.
  • Custom provider / model plumbing — Model picker drops models (#62447), editing limits makes providers vanish (#53005), --model ignored on resume (#61507), Ollama tool calls not executed (#46625).
  • Silent configuration failures — Agent files silently dropped on [-prefixed descriptions (#54200) or ignored permissions when name is present (#62415). No warnings, hard to debug.
  • Session state corruption — Stuck running sessions with unresponsive interrupts and 499 deletes (#62442), /goal stuck after /undo (#62138).
  • Multilingual output corruption — GLM-based free models injecting CJK/Cyrillic glyphs into Slavic-language answers (#57844, #62411).
  • Connectivity instability — Recurring ECONNRESET across all free models (#62179).
  • MCP reliability — OAuth dialog closing mid-flow (#51060) and lost Mcp-Session-Id during parallel calls (#59640).
Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest — 2026-11-07

No new releases in the last 24h.

  1. [#10605] ChatGPT/OpenAI OAuth 403 — "subscription sharing" error (link) — OPEN, 13 comments, 1 👍. Plus-tier users are locked out with a 403 after logout/login. High visibility because it blocks a paid subscription path; no official fix yet.

5. Hot Discussions

Q&A / Ideas

Show and tell

Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Highlights

Qwen Code shipped v0.26.9 stable alongside a fresh nightly, headlined by a major expansion of the Skill installation and activation system (ZIP uploads, daemon APIs, TypeScript SDK support, bulk activation, and recovery protections). Meanwhile, issue activity is dominated by CI stability churn from qwen-code-dev-bot and a cluster of high-severity session-management bugs, including a documented case of auto-compaction turning a review-only skill into unauthorized source-code implementation.

2. Releases

v0.26.9 (stable) and v0.26.9-nightly.20261106.80fd7c3353 both landed in the last 24h.

  • No known breaking changes.
  • Headline feature: Skill installation and activation — Skill ZIP uploads, daemon APIs, TypeScript SDK support, bulk activation, and recovery protections make installing and managing skills substantially more robust.
  • Nightly included test hardening for the interactive foreground-shell (poll the foreground-shell frame instead of snapshotting it, PR #16455).

3. Hot Issues

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate — no test identified (OPEN, 217 comments). A long-running meta-issue tracking a persistently red Managed Agent gate. The extreme comment volume signals chronic CI instability, not a single bug.
  2. #13113 — Session becomes unopenable: "Transcript snapshot is too large to index" (P1). file_history_snapshot grows quadratically and eventually exceeds a hardcoded 256 MiB index limit, making sessions permanently unopenable. A serious data-loss-adjacent bug for long sessions.
  3. #16418 — Repeated auto-compaction turns review-only skill into unauthorized source-code implementation (P1). A /ce-doc-review skill was unexpectedly escalated into implementing the reviewed plan — a notable agent-safety and permission-scope concern.
  4. #15597 — Headless -p managed auto-memory can never save (P1). The implicit edit/write_file deny overrides memory agents' scoped allow, so auto-memory silently no-ops while still costing tokens.
  5. #15412 — Long project paths prevent chat recording and break sessions list (P2). Path flattening exceeds filesystem component limits on macOS.
  6. #15675 — sed edit simulation: . does not match \r or a whole emoji (P1, now CLOSED). In-process sed simulation diverges from real sed due to missing s/u RegExp flags.
  7. #15310 — Tell the model which shell it uses, instead of letting it assume bash (P3). On Windows, the model writes POSIX commands into cmd.exe, burning a full turn per failure.
  8. #15495 — Image payload eviction has no off switch and an undocumented threshold (P2). Silent rewriting of inline images at an undeclared count of 20.
  9. #16457 — MCP OAuth: overlapping flows share fixed callback port 7777 (P2). Starting a second OAuth flow invalidates the first, breaking multi-server authorization.
  10. #14629 — Telemetry: emit OpenRouter routing provider and generation id as span attributes (P3). Strong interest in aggregator-routing observability.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #16501 — refactor(runtime-broker): extract binding provisioning from RuntimeBrokerService. Continues the decomposition of the Runtime Broker into dedicated collaborators (matching the dispatcher/reconciler/recovery pattern).
  2. #16498 — feat(managed-agent): Add execution diagnostics and agent graph. Persists tool/Skill usage, file-operation and line-change metrics, and an authorized agent relationship view — decoupling execution evidence from conversation outcomes.
  3. #16493 — feat(channels): add GitHub repository event filter with allowlist and blocklist. Surfaces a first-class Repository Filter control in the Web Shell channel editor.
  4. #16470 — fix(release): derive the next patch when the preview baseline lags latest. Repairs version resolution when a stable patch shipped after the latest preview.
  5. #16401 — fix(cli): forward the folder-trust store into the container sandbox. Prevents containerized re-execution from falling back to default trust state.
  6. #16352 — fix(managed-agent): mask digit-led passwords and refuse empty Harness user info. Hardening the upgrade command's start/verify phases.
  7. #14353 — fix(web-shell): honor configured loading phrases. Applies custom loading phrases while preserving host overrides and built-in fallback.
  8. #16503 — refactor(managed-agent): fold the last CSI statement helper copies. Removes duplicated statement-preparation helpers in CSI stores.
  9. #15286 — fix(ci): keep sdk-java resolver bookkeeping and in-house jars out of the host cache. Prevents mutable inode sharing between job-local Maven repos and the host cache.
  10. #12592 — fix(session): reattach explicit resume after project move. Adds bounded cross-project lookup so qwen --resume <uuid> survives a moved project directory.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided in the source dataset; this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Better memory & long-term context — optional external memory services (#16429 proposing bzmem), plus fixes to managed auto-memory in headless mode (#15597).
  • Cross-platform correctness — shell-awareness on Windows (#15310), path-length handling on macOS (#15412).
  • Web Shell UX — inline branch chat anchored to selections (#16474), managed-host UI gaps (#16471).
  • Observability & telemetry — OpenRouter routing attributes (#14629), cache-write token preservation (#15414).
  • Session management robustness — transcript indexing limits, resume-after-move, background shell lifecycle.
  • Terminal integration — OSC 7501 program status reporting (#13870).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • CI noise drowning real signal. A large fraction of hot issues are bot-filed Main CI failed reports (e.g. #14724, #16191, #16377), several self-labeled "Provisional." This erodes triage quality and community attention.
  • Session state fragility. Unbounded transcript growth (#13113), path-derived session directories (#15412), and background-shell status files stuck "running" after abrupt ends (#15800) form a recurring cluster.
  • Permission/approval surprises. Auto-memory denial (#15597), auto-compaction escalation (#16418), and amend-guard gaps (#16449) all point to approval logic that behaves unexpectedly under long-running or headless conditions.
  • Cross-platform shell assumptions. Windows users pay a full model turn per failed POSIX-style command (#15310).
  • Stale PR backlog. Multiple [status/stale] PRs from September (e.g. #12592, #12572, #12450) remain unmerged after weeks, suggesting reviewer bandwidth constraints.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-07

Issues: 367 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-07 00:50 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains in a high-tempo maintenance phase: 367 issues and 500 PRs were updated in the last 24 hours, with no new releases cut. The issue mix is heavily weighted toward regressions and state/session-integrity bugs (SQLite worker OOM, MCP lifecycle leaks, Gateway event-loop stalls), suggesting the team is still stabilizing the 2026.10.x–2026.11.x line rather than shipping new surface area. PR throughput is healthy (133 merged/closed vs 367 open), but the open backlog is large and many top-commented issues carry clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr and needs-maintainer-review — meaning fixes exist conceptually but are stuck at review. Community energy is concentrated on a small set of long-lived "diamond lobster" bugs, several of which are P0/P1 crash-loops or memory regressions. Overall project health: active but under stability pressure; the ratio of open-to-merged PRs and the volume of unaddressed P1s are the main watch items.

2. Releases

None. No new releases in the last 24h. (Notable context: issue threads reference in-flight prereleases v2026.11.5-beta.1 and an extended-stable prep PR for 2026.9.37.)

3. Project Progress

133 PRs were merged/closed in the last 24h. Notable closures and active merges include:

  • #194380 [CLOSED] improve(ci): scope provisioning tests to copied inputs — reduces wasteful CI work for source-only PRs. link
  • #194379 [CLOSED] fix(release): authorize scoped 2026.11.2 Kova waiver — unblocks a release perf gate. link
  • #194369 [CLOSED] chore(release): prepare 2026.9.37 extended-stable — backport batch restoring privacy boundaries, session-account continuity, and safer update/state handling on the extended-stable line. link
  • #168794 / #166017 / #164923 [CLOSED issues] — several long-running bug threads closed, including Codex 32 MiB image-request 502s, MCP session idle-TTL non-eviction, and short-term promotion structural rejection. 166017 · 164923
  • #178291 [CLOSED] — post-activation Doctor authority failure on 2026.10.4→10.5 update resolved. link

Net: strong bug-closing cadence on legacy regressions, but new P1/P2s are arriving faster than maintainers can triage (see Backlog Watch).

4. Community Hot Topics

Item Comments Type Link
#160959 Gateway blocks for minutes capturing large external plugins (2026.9.6 regression) 80 P0 crash-loop link
#164294 Gateway state DB WAL auto-checkpoint never completes 39 P2 link
#177656 native host exec returns shared-state integrity-admission error 29 P1 link
#150635 short-term recall eviction blocks dreaming deep-phase promotion 25 P2 link
#191944 gateway stop fails on macOS "ancestry could not be fully inspected" 23 P2 UX link

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs. peers:

  • Scale dominance: OpenClaw's 367 issues / 500 PRs updated in 24h is ~7–10× the volume of Hermes or ZeroClaw and ~13–23× QwenPaw's — it operates at reference-implementation scale, acting as the de facto framework other projects benchmark against.

  • Richer subsystem surface: Dream Diary, Doctor authority model, Gateway event-loop integrity, and MCP lifecycle handling represent deeper subsystem investment than peer projects.

Technical approach differences:

  • Gateway-centric architecture with explicit session-admission semantics and a SQLite worker pool — a heavier footprint than Hermes' gateway/session-authority consolidation or QwenPaw's plugin-per-channel model.
  • Prerelease/beta channeling (v2026.11.5-beta.1, 2026.9.37 extended-stable) — peers ship on simpler stable/beta splits.
  • Dependency on native host exec and cloud-worker turns introduces integrity-admission failure classes (#177656, #182647) unique to its breadth.

Community size comparison:

  • OpenClaw's top issue threads carry 80, 39, 29, 25, 23 comments vs. Hermes' peak of 40, QwenPaw's 4, and ZeroClaw's 9. This is a 10–20× larger engaged user base at the top of the funnel.
  • Caveat: Zero 👍 on most high-comment OpenClaw issues vs. modest 👍 counts on Hermes (#97681: 4) and QwenPaw — OpenClaw's engagement is issue-driven and problem-centric, not enthusiasm-driven, suggesting a user base dependent on it operationally rather than passionately.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Three cross-project requirements emerge as ecosystem-wide:

(a) Session/State Integrity Under Load — OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw

  • OpenClaw: SQLite worker OOM (#191847), Gateway event-loop stalls (#160959), admission-closed failures (#182647).
  • Hermes: Prompt lost on attached clients (#147626), Stop reporting false cancellation (#143303), composer restore-after-send (#148277).
  • ZeroClaw: Long-session 422 rejections (#12263), channel startup message overwrite (#12279).
  • Need: Atomic, re-checkable authority over session state that survives retries, reconnects, and multi-device attachment.

(b) Memory Subsystem Correctness — OpenClaw, Hermes, QwenPaw

  • OpenClaw: Recall eviction blocking dreaming promotion (#150635), eviction-before-promotion defects.
  • Hermes: Memory/kanban read-only API demand (#149815); recall semantics in multisession flows.
  • QwenPaw: Memory tag index 503 (#8580), reranker empty-api_key errors (#8276), refactor of recall as transient context (#8457).
  • Need: Deterministic index rebuild, safe eviction policy, and clear separation between persisted memory and injected recall.

(c) Authorization/Identity Boundaries — OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw

  • OpenClaw: Shared-state integrity admission (#177656/#182647), MCP lifecycle leaks.
  • Hermes: Approval-gate bypass via shell functions (#150329), toolset pick ignored on gateway path (#147832).
  • ZeroClaw: A concentrated 10+ issue security sweep — session ownership (#11127), SOP wildcards (#11123), cron approval (#12260), XFF spoofing (#12052), vodozemac CVEs (#12272).
  • Need: Authority re-validated at each effect using trusted runtime facts, not caller-supplied data.

(d) Plugin/MCP Contract Hardening — Hermes, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw, OpenClaw

  • Hermes: Plugin Hackathon cluster + catalog PRs (~5), but registration/nav regressions.
  • QwenPaw: Plugin metadata failures (#8595), navigation regression (#8590), dependency check refactor (#8598).
  • ZeroClaw: Multi-registry origins (#12216), deferred MCP HashMap ordering (#12176).
  • Need: Durable plugin manifest/route contracts as the ecosystem scales to hundreds of community extensions.

7. Trend Signals

Five industry-level signals valuable to AI agent developers:

1. Identity/Authorization is the new correctness frontier

ZeroClaw's dedicated 10+ issue security sweep, Hermes' approval-gate bypass (#150329), and OpenClaw's shared-state admission failures all point to the same conclusion: the next generation of agent bugs will be authority-boundary bugs, not inference-quality bugs. Actionable for developers: design authority checks as atomic, per-effect, trusted-fact-based operations from day one.

2. Session integrity across multi-device/multi-channel is table stakes

Every active project reports session-state inconsistencies under attach/retry/reconnect. Users are becoming SREs for their own agents. Actionable: invest early in idempotent turn semantics and cross-client session reconciliation.

3. Memory subsystems need explicit "trusted vs. synthetic" separation

QwenPaw #8457 (recall injected as untrusted context), OpenClaw's dream/recall eviction defects, and Hermes' memory API requests all converge on: memory is not a single abstraction — index, eviction, and recall-injection are separate, independently testable concerns.

4. Plugin/MCP registration contracts are scaling bottlenecks

Three of four active projects report plugin metadata/route/manifest failures. Actionable: publish and version a plugin contract spec now, before the ecosystem reaches hundreds of extensions.

5. Release gating has shifted from feature-completeness to security- and integrity-completeness

ZeroClaw's v0.9.0 is explicitly security-gated; OpenClaw is holding back 2026.12 feature candidates behind stability backports. Actionable for developers: plan security/integrity review as a release gate, not a post-release patch cycle — this is becoming the ecosystem norm.

  • Issue #8592 — Creator review round becomes permanently undecidable; REJECT always returns 422 "visual artifact reference references missing id" (plus 502 on expired provider source_url, frame_stats ignoring CREATOR_FFMPEG_PATH). No fix PR yet. Bundles three defects.

🟠 High — Platform-specific breakage:

  • Issue #8595 — Plugin install fails with "No package metadata was found" for qwenpaw-creator v2.0.4 via both UI and CLI.
  • Issue #8517 — Hub Docker runtime fails with Permission denied on working/config.json when Hub runs as non-root.

🟡 Medium — Functional regressions:

  • Issue #8576 — Default agent edit button disabled in console although PUT API allows editing. Fix PR open: #8608.

🟢 Low / already fixed today: Issues #8596, #8276, #8549, #8533, #8365, #8516, #8590 all closed with corresponding PRs.

Stability trend: Windows-specific path handling and non-root Docker deployments are emerging as a recurring cluster of environment-sensitive failures — a notable risk for the desktop/self-hosted user base.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Active feature requests and their likely trajectory:

Request Issue/PR Likelihood in next release
Quote response text in follow-ups #5110 → PR #8609 open High — PR already submitted
Compact tool_call_format for IM channels #7436 → PR #8610 open High — PR already submitted
Browser tab title follows session name #8605 Medium — no PR yet, low-complexity
Creator UI usability overhaul #8591 Medium — depends on Creator stability track (#8592)
Delete mode for model management PR #8611 open High — PR open
Reranker model center w/ precision history PR #8472 open Medium — larger XXL PR

Prediction: The next patch/beta is likely to bundle the console UX trio (quote-to-follow-up, tool-call compaction, model deletion) plus the default-agent editing fix (#8608), since all now have open or submitted PRs. The memory subsystem (reranker center #8472, tag index rebuild #8580) appears to be the next larger investment area.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points expressed:

  • Console/UI friction dominates: Users report unidentifiable UI elements (white-on-white buttons in Creator, #8591), all browser tabs showing identical titles (#8605), and disabled edit buttons that contradict backend capabilities (#8576). This suggests a UI polish gap in the 2.3.0b2 beta.
  • Deployment friction: Offline/air-gapped installs (#1453, closed after 8 months) and non-root Docker (#8517) reveal that self-hosting is a meaningful — and sometimes neglected — use case.
  • Plugin ecosystem immaturity: Two separate plugin failures reported today (#8595 metadata, #8590 navigation regression) indicate the plugin registration/route contract needs hardening.
  • Cross-platform reliability: Windows users hit multiple distinct issues (#8585 path canonicalization, #8603 provider tool calls), suggesting Windows is under-tested relative to Linux/macOS.

Satisfaction signals: Rapid issue triage (many same-day or next-day closures) and PRs appearing within hours of feature requests (#8609, #8610) indicate a responsive maintainer team, which likely buoys community sentiment despite the bug volume.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered or high-impact items needing maintainer attention:

  • Issue #8580 — Memory tag index 503. Opened 2026-11-04, 4 comments, no fix PR, no maintainer label visible. This is a core memory feature completely broken; it deserves prioritization.
  • Issue #8592 — Creator review round permanently undecidable. No fix PR. Author explicitly offered to split into three issues — maintainers should respond to triage.
  • Issue #8585 — Windows recall_history SQLite URI breakage. No fix PR, 2 comments. Cross-version regression affecting all Windows desktop users.
  • Issue #8517 — Hub Docker non-root permission denied. Open since 2026-10-31, 3 comments, no PR. Blocks containerized deployments.
  • Issue #1453 — CoPaw offline install; closed today after ~8 months — worth reviewing the resolution to ensure the underlying offline-model-connection limitation is documented, not just closed.
  • PR #8234 — GBK/CP936 decoding fix for read/edit/grep. Open since 2026-10-14 (XXL size), under review. Addresses silent data loss on Chinese Windows — high user impact, needs review bandwidth.

Health assessment: The project is actively maintained with fast turnaround on low-complexity issues, but larger architectural items (memory indexing, Creator pipeline, Windows path handling, plugin contracts) are accumulating without dedicated fix PRs. Maintainer attention should prioritize the memory tag 503 and Creator undecidable review as the two highest-severity unresolved blockers.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw is in a high-velocity security-hardening phase ahead of the v0.9.0 release. Activity remains intense: 20 issues touched in the last 24h (14 closed, 6 open) and 50 PRs updated (15 merged/closed, 35 open), with no new releases. The dominant theme is a systematic sweep of principal/identity-access boundary bugs — session ownership, SOP authorization, rate-limit keying, and cron approval — largely driven by contributors IftekharUddin and JordanTheJet, with review support from Audacity88. The project's health signal is mixed-positive: many p1/high-risk security bugs are being closed quickly, but new follow-up issues keep surfacing from those same fixes, suggesting the authorization model is undergoing a deep, layered refactor rather than isolated patching. Release notes (v0.9.0 tags) appear on many security issues, indicating this work is gating the next version.

2. Releases

None. No new releases in the last 24h. Note, however, that many open PRs and issues are tagged release:v0.9.0, implying an upcoming release is accumulating a substantial security and identity-access payload.

3. Project Progress

15 PRs were merged/closed today. Highlights:

  • #12273 [CLOSED] — fix(deps): update vodozemac to 0.11.2 for RUSTSEC-2026-0445 and -0451. Unblocks the Quality Gate Security job and every PR by patching two fresh RustSec advisories. (link)
  • #12233 [CLOSED] — fix(gateway): limit and cap OIDC bearer verification on the config route group. Adds attempt ledger and in-flight caps to stop identity-provider amplification. (link)
  • #12114 [CLOSED] — fix(gateway): key rate limits on the proxy-appended XFF hop. Fixes loopback-exemption spoofing via X-Forwarded-For. (link)
  • Closed issues: #11127 (session-data ownership bypass), #11123 (SOP wildcard tool selectors), #12051 (SOP workshop shared authorship), #12046 (wildcard principal-unaware tools), #12047 (OIDC limiter), #12052 (XFF keying), #12272 (vodozemac advisories), #11962 (daemon RPC session leak at cap 64), #12178, #12176 (deferred MCP HashMap ordering), #12155 (quickstart false "no config written"), #12217 (email docs), #12248, #12249.

Features advanced:

  • #10315 Phase 2 (relay-served web dashboard) — PR #12270 + placement-exception doc PR #12274 open.
  • Multi-model provider profiles — long-running foundational PR #9809 still open.
  • Telegram voice replies (PR #12276) and paired-device voice settings (PR #12269) moving.
  • Multi-origin plugin registries (PR #12216) progressing.

4. Community Hot Topics

  • #9746 [OPEN] — fix(tools): per-agent ownership scoping for session tools and discord_search (link) — the highest-scrutiny PR today; a large (size:XL) identity-access refactor that spawned multiple follow-up issues (#12282 documents its placement exception). Still open and needs-author-action.
  • #10926 [OPEN] — Matrix send_via treats peer user identities as room destinations (link) — 9 comments, still unresolved after ~7 weeks; the highest-comment issue in the window and a signal of channel-routing model confusion.
  • #11127 / #11123 / #12046 / #12051 [CLOSED] — the security-boundary cluster; each closed with only 2–3 comments, indicating fix-first, low-discussion resolution.
  • #12239 [OPEN] — fix(rpc): hold current authority through session effects (link) — p1/high-risk, follow-up to #11234; central to the authorization-model refactor.

Underlying need: contributors are converging on a single principle — authority must be re-checked atomically at each effect, using trusted facts (runtime identity, live config) rather than caller-supplied data. Reviewer attention is clustering on three PRs (#9746, #12239, #11149) that together would enforce this consistently.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (all dated 2026-11-06 unless noted):

  • S1 — workflow blocked: #12263 [OPEN] — Strict provider permanently rejects a long tool-heavy session (422 missing field tool_call_id) once outbound request size diverges from stored session. No fix PR yet; conversation becomes unusable. (link)
  • S1 — workflow blocked: #12272 [CLOSED] — vodozemac RUSTSEC advisories fail CI on every PR. Fixed by PR #12273. (link)
  • S2 — #12260 [OPEN] — RPC cron/add and cron/patch treat the caller as an operator approval for shell commands (approved = true). Open fix in PR #11149. (link)
  • S2 — #12279 [OPEN] — Channel startup caps a long transcript from an earlier read, overwriting a message appended in between (possible data loss; triage may escalate to S0). (link)
  • S2 — #10926 [OPEN] — Matrix send_via peer-identity/room-destination confusion. (link)
  • S2 — #11962 [CLOSED] — Daemon's 64 live RPC sessions never released when idle; remote clients can exhaust them. Fixed. (link)
  • S3 — #12155 [CLOSED] — Quickstart claims "No config written" but ~/.zeroclaw/config.toml exists. Fixed. (link)

Assessment: the resolved set outweighs the open set, and every open S1/S2 now has a linked fix PR except #12263 and #12279. That latter pair — plus the security cluster — should be watched before v0.9.0.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Strong signals that the following are likely in v0.9.0 or immediately after, given release:v0.9.0 tags and active PRs:

  • Relay-served daemon web dashboard (PR #12270, doc #12274) — closes a real browser-access gap for relay-connected daemons.
  • Multiple models per provider profile (PR #9809) — large provider-layer rework with capability tagging, presets, and fallback.
  • Telegram voice replies synthesized during text generation (PR #12276) and paired-device voice settings (PR #12269).
  • Multi-registry plugin origins (PR #12216) — enables private + public registry coexistence.
  • Local MCP configuration controls (PR #12275) — explicit, deferred-write config edits by an authorized agent.
  • SOP cancel loopback hardening (issue #12280 → PR #12281).

Prediction: v0.9.0 will ship as a security + identity-access release first, with the dashboard/relay and provider-model features riding alongside if their XL PRs clear review.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Pain point — long-session fragility: #12263 and #12279 both describe data loss or permanent conversation breakage in long, tool-heavy or transcript-restore scenarios. This is the most user-visible stability risk.
  • Pain point — proxy/deployment misconfiguration: #12052 (XFF loopback spoofing) reflects real operator confusion about running ZeroClaw behind reverse proxies. The fix plus docs will matter for self-hosters.
  • Pain point — onboarding polish: #12155 shows quickstart messaging erodes trust ("No config written" while a config file is written).
  • Satisfaction signal: security issues #11127, #11123, #12046, #12051 were all reported from source review and closed promptly, suggesting a responsive maintainer/security review loop.
  • Dissatisfaction signal: #9746 has been open since 2026-08-04 and still carries needs-author-action, indicating the community-authored ownership-scoping fix is being slowed by review latency.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention due to age, size, or review stalls:

  • #9746 [OPEN since 2026-08-04] — per-agent ownership scoping (XL, p1, high risk, needs-author-action, release-gate). The single most consequential stalled PR; multiple closed issues depend on its landing. (link)
  • #9809 [OPEN since 2026-08-07] — multiple models per provider profile (XL, needs-author-action). Foundational provider work blocked on author action. (link)
  • #11149 [OPEN since 2026-09-26] — enforce cron approval and authority at the write (XL, high risk). Directly relevant to open bug #12260 and to the v0.9.0 security payload. (link)
  • #10926 [OPEN since 2026-09-17] — Matrix send_via destination bug; 9 comments, no fix PR, follow-up + risk:medium. (link)
  • #12239 [OPEN] — hold current authority through session effects (p1, needs-maintainer-review); gateway/security surface that gates v0.9.0. (link)

Overall health: active and security-focused, with fast closure of high-severity findings but a growing set of stacked follow-ups. The main risk to v0.9.0 is review throughput on three XL PRs (#9746, #9809, #11149) rather than a shortage of fixes. Recommend prioritizing maintainer review of #12239 and #11149 to close the remaining S2 authorization gaps (#12260) and unblock the release.

item.content:encoded:
AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-11-07

Generated: 2026-11-07 00:50 UTC | Projects covered: 6

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

Cross-Project Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — AI Infrastructure Ecosystem

Digest date: 2026-11-07

1. Ecosystem Overview

Today's activity reflects a maturing but still unstable inference stack: no project shipped a major release in the last 24 hours, yet every tracker shows heavy PR/issue churn concentrated on correctness regressions in hybrid-attention and MoE models (vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp all report silent KV/quant corruption), P/D disaggregation correctness (vLLM NixlConnector, SGLang PP deadlocks), and long-context agent workloads (reasoning parsers, tool-call streaming, gateway state). Performance work has shifted from raw kernel wins toward weight-load latency (SGLang's sub-second Weight Cache Daemon), CPU/GPU memory accounting (Ollama runner leaks, llama.cpp ClassLRU MoE cache), and speculative-decoding verification across AMDs, Vulkan, and OpenCL. Meanwhile, gateway and training layers (LiteLLM, Unsloth) are absorbing the fallout of upstream regressions via adapter-level backports and Studio-side UX fixes. The net signal is a stack where model/architecture coverage is racing ahead of correctness guarantees, and operators are being asked to validate per-model rather than per-version.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Layer Releases (24h) Issue Activity PR Activity Dominant Theme
vLLM Serving engine None (0.32.0 backlog burn-down) High — NixlConnector #61229, GDN+PP #63505, int8_per_token_head #50702/#50749 Heavy — MoE quant fixes, Rust frontend tool-call streaming, XPU MoE Correctness in disaggregation + hybrid models
SGLang Serving engine None Very high — coredump tracker (#26340, 356 comments), CI flaky tracker (#42752, 186) Active — DSV4.1 FP8 MegaAttention, DSA packed prefill, AMD MTP verify FP8 KV scale bug #48749 is top-of-stack
llama.cpp Local runtime 9 builds (b12170–b12180) Moderate — Vulkan coopmat #31560, RAM cache #27148, CUDA IMA #31077 Active across Hexagon/Vulkan/OpenCL/WebGPU Kimi-K3.1-Pro landing + backend tuning
Ollama Local runtime None (0.40.x line) High — Vulkan/iGPU crashes #19558, #19158, #19589 Moderate — runner leak #19581, Claude Code routing #19587 Post-migration regression on AMD/Intel
LiteLLM Gateway v1.108.2 (LTS patch) High — Gemini stream corruption #25869, tool drop #48145, cache_control #47046 Very high — LTS backports from mateo-berri LTS consolidation + agent-loop correctness
Unsloth Training/Fine-tuning v0.1.916-beta High — 39 updated; Krea crash #16892, multi-GPU #16925 High — Studio P1 perf, MCP break, chat-template fix Desktop/Studio UX + transformers 5.23 migration

Reading the table: shipping velocity is inversely correlated with scope — llama.cpp ships daily builds for a single-node runtime; vLLM/SGLang, operating at cluster scale, are burning down long-tail correctness before cutting releases. LiteLLM is the only project actively running a backport branch ahead of main, signaling that LTS consumers are its priority over main-trackers.

3. Model Support Race

Architecture support is no longer a moat — correctness is.

Architecture / Model vLLM SGLang llama.cpp Ollama LiteLLM Unsloth
DeepSeek-V4.1 (Engram, SP+PP, FP8 MegaAttn) ✅ Engram offload #62238, SP+PP #65766 ✅ FP8 MegaAttention #48926 — — ✅ catalog add —
Kimi-K3.1-Pro (DSA sparse attention) — — ✅ b12180 spec + conversion — ⚠️ requested, closed without impl (#33921) —
Qwen3.8 family (GDN hybrid, QSA cache) ✅ Rust frontend tool-call #66198; GDN bug #63505 ✅ QSA cache sharding #43527 — ✅ MLX mixed-precision #18078 — —
Gemma 4 ✅ Rust tool-call streaming #66199 — ✅ prefill gains #31356; MTP IMA #31077 ✅ tool-arg fix #19274 — ✅ chat-template reasoning fix #16699
GLM-5.3-Flash ✅ P/D GB200 issue #55434 ⚠️ degeneration #36669 ✅ CUDA IMA #28282 — — —
Nemotron 3.5 ASR / dense ⚠️ ASR request #47455 — — ❌ dense gap #19566 — —
Cosmos3 (video) — — — — ✅ OpenRouter video fields #50319 ✅ Edge/Nano, Sim-Transfer #16737/16741/16975
MiMo-V2 / MageVL ✅ timestamp fix #66201 — ✅ MageVL #31819 — — —

Who's ahead:

  • vLLM leads on frontier serving breadth — first to land DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram offload, MXFP4 packed tables, and sequence-parallel + PP combinations. But its headline wins are on hardware most users don't yet run (SM120).
  • llama.cpp leads on conversion/locality — Kimi-K3.1-Pro (a DSA-sparse architecture) landed with converter + tests on day one, and PLE shard loading (#31185) shows a push toward composable GGUF layouts.
  • Unsloth leads on creative/multimodal generation — Cosmos3 workflows (continuation, restyle) and AI-agent integration (Claude Agent connection #16963) are unique to it.
  • LiteLLM is the strategic aggregator — its value is catalog depth (Baseten, CoreWeave Forge, Foundry Local, OpenRouter video), not model architecture engineering.

Watchpoint: Kimi-K3 (Moonshot) and Tinker remain closed-without-implementation on LiteLLM (#33921) — a real gap for teams standardizing on gateway-fronted frontier models.

4. Performance Frontier

Optimization effort has fragmented across five loci, with diminishing returns near single-node hardware:

(a) KV cache & memory management — the most active frontier.

  • vLLM: int8_per_token_head scale-view fill corrupting GDN state (#63944); batch-invariant mode routing Linear to Triton unnecessarily on Hopper/Blackwell (#65569).
  • SGLang: Weight Cache Daemon Phase 1 (#33522) — 306–327s → <1s weight loads on Qwen3-235B FP8 is the single largest latency win reported today.
  • llama.cpp: ClassLRU MoE expert cache (#31233) changes eviction semantics; RAM prompt cache correctness (#27148) is a liability.
  • Unsloth: idle-unload reload fidelity (#16927) — preserving KV dtype/context across unload.

(b) Batching & scheduling

  • vLLM: TRT-LLM monolithic MoE skips padded rows under DP (#65972); encoder CUDA graphs simplify replay (#65227).
  • SGLang: DSA packed prefill top-k to CUDA (#45891); AMD MTP rejection-sampling verify drops vocab-wide sort (#48090).
  • Ollama: scheduler VRAM accounting fix (#19585), runner-leak fix (#19581).

(c) Quantization

  • Diverging: vLLM lands MXFP4-packed Engram tables (#61530) and lifts QuIP Hadamard TP (#65732); SGLang's FP8 KV scales silently ignored (#48749) is a correctness regression, not a perf gain.
  • llama.cpp NVFP4 on Blackwell (#23572) closed — native FP4 MMA at Q4_0 footprint.

(d) Distributed serving

  • vLLM: GDN+PP=3 on sm_86 (#63505), TP4+EP regression on MiniMax-M2.7 (#63705), SP+PP enablement for DeepSeek-V4 (#65766).
  • SGLang: PP disaggregated prefill deadlock on abort storms (#34572, closed w/ RCA).

(e) Kernels & backends

  • MoE dominates: SM12x alignment regression (#58624), DeepSeek shared-expert FP16 division (#65842), XPU XE3P grouped GEMM (#60609), ROCm wvSplitK (#63725).
  • Non-CUDA catching up: Hexagon CONV_3D (#31814), KleidiAI SME2 for ARM FA (#29394), OpenCL small-n GEMV (#31831), Vulkan readonly decodeBuf (#31833).

Verdict: The frontier has moved from "make it faster on H100" to "make it correct on the hardware people actually own" — SM120s, MI355X, Intel Arc, Strix Halo, Apple Silicon.

5. Layer Positioning

The six projects map cleanly onto four distinct layers, with notable overlaps at the edges:

Layer Project(s) Primary consumer Moat
Cluster serving engine vLLM, SGLang Platform/infra teams, Kubernetes operators Kernel breadth, disaggregation, cluster-scale scheduling
Local runtime llama.cpp, Ollama Desktop/server hobbyists, edge deployments, privacy-sensitive apps Hardware ubiquity, conversion tooling, quantization variety
LLM gateway LiteLLM App/agent teams, platform API teams Provider/catalog breadth, budget, observability, LTS discipline
Training / fine-tuning Unsloth Model builders, small fine-tuning teams LoRA efficiency, Studio UX, GGUF export

Distinctions that matter:

  • vLLM vs SGLang: vLLM is breadth-first (more models, more backends, expandable frontend in Rust); SGLang is depth-first on a narrower set of frontier models (DeepSeek, Qwen3.8, GLM) with tighter kernel integration and a documented, prioritized stability ladder (their digest ranks severity explicitly).
  • llama.cpp vs Ollama: llama.cpp is the engine-of-record for portability; Ollama is the UX layer on top. Ollama's 0.40.x migration to llama-server as the runner is the reason its stability issues now track upstream builds — meaning Ollama regressions frequently mirror llama.cpp build regressions, delayed.
  • LiteLLM's positioning has shifted — it's no longer a routing shim but a compatibility normalization layer, absorbing provider quirks (Gemini thought_signatures, Anthropic server_tool_use, Bedrock reasoning replay). For agent teams, it's the abstraction that decides whether your tool loop works.
  • Unsloth is the only project spanning training → inference (train LoRA → export GGUF → run in Studio/llama.cpp). This vertical integration is its moat, but it also means it inherits upstream runtime risk.

Overlap risk: SGLang's MindIE-SD RFC (#48582) and USE for FlashInfer-style plugins, plus vLLM's Rust frontend, suggest serving engines and gateways are beginning to blur — vLLM may absorb functionality currently delegated to LiteLLM.

6. Trend Signals

T1 — Hybrid-attention is the new correctness frontier. GDN, DSA, QSA, MLA, MoE-with-shared-experts appear in six separate correctness bugs across vLLM, SGLang, and llama.cpp today. Pre-hybrid, attention was uniform and correctness was tractable; post-hybrid, each architecture has its own cache/scale/prefix-caching interaction matrix.

T2 — Silent corruption is the dominant failure mode. #61229 (NixlConnector KV), #48749 (FP8 KV scales), #27148 (RAM cache cross-contamination), #50702 (int8_per_token_head) all produce plausible output while being wrong. This is qualitatively worse than crashes — it defeats canary throughput benchmarking.

T3 — Disaggregated P/D is still not production-safe. vLLM's NixlConnector lease expiry (#61229), SGLang's PP deadlock on aborts (#34572), and llama.cpp's roadmap item #21266 all indicate that disaggregation is the most-discussed feature and the least-trustworthy, in the same cycle.

T4 — Weight-load latency is the new cold-start battleground. SGLang's sub-second weight cache, Unsloth's idle-unload fidelity, and Ollama's VRAM leak fix all serve the same pattern: trainer→engine sync, LoRA hot-swap, multi-tenant redeploys. The era of "load once, serve forever" is ending.

T5 — Agent-loop correctness is increasingly a gateway concern. LiteLLM is absorbing bugs that originate in provider streaming semantics (Gemini thought signatures, Anthropic server_tool_use, OpenRouter empty choices, Bedrock reasoning replay). Agent developers should expect their gateway, not their LLM, to be the loop-breaking component.

T6 — Non-NVIDIA hardware is a first-class citizen — with growing regression surface. Vulkan coopmat nondeterminism on Intel Arc (#31560), Ollama iGPU load crashes (#19558/#19158/#19589), ROCm gfx1151 OOM (#64098), SM12x MoE regression (#58624). The portability win is real; the QA cost is real too.

What Agent / Application Developers Should Do This Week

  1. Pin per-model, not per-version. No engine is "safe at vX.Y.Z" today — safety is per (engine, model, hardware, prefix-caching-state) tuple. Build a per-model canary eval that checks output identity, not throughput.
  2. Bisect any output drift by toggling prefix caching first. Bugs #63505, #50702, #51771, #27148 all surface only with prefix caching on.
  3. Validate disaggregated deployments against a non-disaggregated baseline before upgrading. #61229 will not raise an error.
  4. On gateways, test multi-turn tool loops daily on your primary model — not just the connector. LiteLLM items 1–9 in §5 have no fix PRs; several are stale.
  5. Exploit the weight-load wins. If you redeploy frequently, SGLang's Weight Cache Daemon (#33522) is currently the largest operational win on the board.
  6. For desktop/edge: pin to last-known-good — llama.cpp b12180 (Kimi-K3.1-Pro), Ollama 0.34.4 for AMD/Intel iGPU users, Unsloth v0.1.916-beta for long-chat UX, transformers <5.23.
  7. Watch the LiteLLM lts tag — fixes are landing there ahead of main; if your team tracks main, you are actively diverging from the supported path.

Per-Project Reports

vLLM — vllm-project/vllm

vLLM Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Highlights

No releases in the past 24h, but issue and PR activity is heavy and concentrated on three themes: KV-cache correctness in disaggregated/hybrid deployments (NixlConnector lease expiry, int8_per_token_head corruption, Qwen3.8 GDN + PP), a cluster of MoE quantization/scaling fixes (DeepSeek shared-expert FP16 division, TRT-LLM DP padding, SM12x DeepGEMM alignment regression), and continued maturation of the Rust frontend, which now has streaming tool-call argument support landing for Gemma 4 and Qwen Coder. Two closed bugs (#63944, #56900) and one closed release-blocker (#59203 → #60762) indicate the maintainers are actively burning down the 0.32.0 regression backlog.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

None. No new tags in the last 24h. Note that #59203 (block-size failures on the v0.32.0 release tag for DeepSeek V4.1 on SM120) was closed today with the fix tracked in #60762 — users on v0.32.0 with SM120 hardware should track that PR before pinning.

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram offload — PR #62238 adds disk offload for ~197 GB Engram tables on memory-constrained nodes (Strix Halo, DGX Spark); PR #61530 adds MXFP4-packed Engram embedding tables (E2M1 + UE8M0 block-32 scales). PR #62238 · PR #61530
  • DeepSeek-V4 sequence parallelism with PP — PR #65766 enables SP for MegaMoE + EP + TP>1 when pipeline parallelism is active (previously disabled for PP>1). PR #65766
  • NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming (nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b, 600M multilingual streaming ASR) — feature request open. Issue #47455
  • Intel XPU MoE — PR #60609 aligns XpuFusedMoe weight/scale layout with vllm-xpu-kernels XE3P grouped GEMM; PR #46871 continues the XPU all-to-all EP backend for batched MoE. PR #60609 · PR #46871
  • Compressed-tensors TP for block-diagonal Hadamard — PR #65732 lifts the NotImplementedError on QuIP-style online Hadamard transforms with TP>1. PR #65732

4. Performance & Optimization

  • SM12x MoE decode regression — ~15% slower since #56876 because get_theoretical_mk_alignment_for_contiguous_layout returns 128 instead of 64 on SM12x. Open, no fix PR yet. Issue #58624
  • MiniMax-M2.7 throughput regression — TP4 + EP degraded across v0.29/0.31/0.32. Issue #63705
  • Batch-invariant mode on Hopper/Blackwell routes Linear layers to Triton even though cuBLAS is already batch-invariant under the mode's settings — unnecessary overhead. Issue #65569
  • GLM-5.3 P/D on GB200 — NIXL submission of 91k–120k KV descriptors per TP-rank transfer dominates over fabric bandwidth, making MNNVL/cuda_ipc slower than RDMA on this workload. Issue #55434
  • DSpark sampling — PR #64476 fuses Markov bias and block combine into Gumbel sampling (split from #63232). PR #64476
  • Encoder (ViT) CUDA graphs — PR #65227 replaces greedy power-of-2 replay splitting with one replay per batch and a finer grid. PR #65227

5. Stability & Regressions

Critical

  • NixlConnector silent KV corruption (#61229, OPEN) — with the pull flow, producer releases KV blocks on lease expiry while a remote READ is in flight; decode silently consumes overwritten KV. This is a correctness-silent failure in P/D disaggregation (UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_copy, vLLM 0.30.0). No fix PR referenced. Issue #61229
  • Qwen3.8-27B GDN hybrid + PP=3 on sm_86 (#63505, OPEN) — Xid 31 illegal memory access with prefix caching, gibberish without it; regression since v0.28.0 affecting v0.31.0 and v0.32.0. Issue #63505
  • DeepSeek-V4-Flash EAGLE/MTP + prefix caching (#51771, OPEN) — untested for hybrid models with ≥3 attention groups; prior fix #33524 only covered the 2-group GPT-OSS shape. Issue #51771

High

  • TP worker hang → EngineDeadError (#41530, OPEN, 8 👍) — DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP=8, MTP speculative decoding; sample_tokens RPC timeout. Issue #41530
  • int8_per_token_head KV corruption — two related reporters: #50702 (prefix caching + 100% KV pool, Gemma-4 hybrid) and #50749 (first generated tokens corrupt when prefix caching is disabled). A root-cause was already identified in #63944 (CLOSED): scale-view fill overwrites Gated DeltaNet state in hybrid models. Issue #50702 · Issue #50749 · Issue #63944
  • Marlin MoE output depends on within-expert token ordering (#52525, OPEN) — batch-invariance violation, relevant to anyone relying on deterministic outputs. Issue #52525
  • Qwen3.5-9B GDN + dynamic LoRA on H20 → NaN (#52568, OPEN) — punica Triton kernel bug, long sequences. Issue #52568
  • DeepSeek MoE shared-expert FP16 division — PR #65842 fixes #65533: since #35949 the MoE runner divides shared expert output by routed_scaling_factor in FP16 for any model setting apply_routed_scale_to_output=True, which is only correct for decoder-compensating families. PR #65842

Moderate

  • Responses API previous_response_id (#43244, OPEN) — drops function_call/function_call_output from stored context. Directly affects agent loops using the Responses API. Issue #43244
  • ROCm GLM-5.2 MTP on MI355X (#52833, CLOSED) — 0% draft acceptance; EP disable triggers hipErrorIllegalAddress.
  • ROCm gfx1151 OOM — PR #64098 bounds DeepSeek V4 DSpark long-run memory growth that previously killed Ray workers. PR #64098
  • Step5 MTP + PP — PR #66000 fixes startup re-validation of the draft config view. PR #66000

Also closed today: #56900 (Qwen1.5-MoE degenerate output under torch.compile on H100 — resolved).

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • P/D disaggregation is not yet safe to trust blindly. #61229 is a silent-corruption class bug — the wrong KV is read, tokens are still emitted, and nothing errors. If you run disaggregated prefill/decode with NixlConnector over TCP/UCX, validate outputs against a non-disaggregated baseline before upgrading, and follow the tracking issue #63149 (KV event correctness across Dynamo, llm-d, and vLLM Router).
  • Hybrid-attention models dominate the risk surface. GDN, DSpark, MLA + DSA, MoE-with-shared-experts, and EAGLE/MTP all have open correctness or regression reports this cycle. Keep per-model canary evals (not just throughput benchmarks) before promoting new vLLM versions.
  • Prefix caching interacts with many of these bugs. #63505, #50702, #51771 all reproduce only (or differently) with prefix caching on. If you see subtle output drift after an upgrade, toggling prefix caching is a fast bisect.
  • If you're building agents: the Responses API state bug (#43244) can silently break multi-turn tool loops when using previous_response_id. Prefer passing full message history or verify your stored-context round-trip. Watch PR #64654 for an ID-only logging mode that preserves request correlation without logging content — useful for gateway-side observability.
  • Tool-calling streaming on Rust frontend is arriving: PRs #66198 (Qwen Coder) and #66199 (Gemma 4) push string argument fragments earlier rather than buffering to end-of-call. This reduces time-to-first-argument for agent UIs; both are gated behind VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1.
  • Quantization users on SM12x / MiniMax / GLM-5.3 should hold or pin until #58624 and #63705 are resolved — both are live throughput regressions with no merged fix.

llama.cpp Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Highlights

Model coverage expanded with Kimi-K3.1-Pro (DSA replacing full-attention MLA on 24 of 93 layers) landing in b12180, alongside a wave of backend tuning across Hexagon, Vulkan, OpenCL and WebGPU. On the stability side, the most notable open items are a Vulkan KHR_coopmat nondeterminism bug on Intel Arc B70 and a RAM-backed prompt cache correctness issue that can cross-contaminate conversations under concurrent load — both matter for production deployments. The disaggregated prefill/decode roadmap item (#21266) remains the most-discussed open feature at 35 comments.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

Nine builds shipped in 24h (b12170–b12180). No hard API breaks, but two behavioural changes worth noting:

  • b12180 — new model architecture support (Kimi-K3.1-Pro); no migration needed for existing models. PR #31779
  • b12177 — CLI no longer crashes on invalid UTF-8 in prompts or files. Commit/PR #31563
  • b12174 — CMake now generates the Windows RC file directly instead of templating win-app.rc.in. Build-system only. PR #31718
  • b12170 — MoE expert cache replaced with a LRFU/MQ-inspired hybrid (ClassLRU). This changes expert eviction behaviour; benchmark before/after if you rely on --n-cpu-moe / MoE offload. PR #31233
  • b12171 — Vulkan now detects ReBAR support and avoids BAR allocations when unavailable. Users with ReBAR disabled may see changed allocation behaviour. PR #31658
  • In flight: #31377 proposes removing the silent n_ctx_slot cap at n_ctx_train, allowing --ctx-size above training context. If merged, this is a semantic change for anyone relying on silent clamping.

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • Kimi-K3.1-Pro text model (b12180) — K3 variant where 24/93 layers use DeepSeek-style lightning indexer attention (32 heads × 128, top_k 2048, no RoPE); KDA linear-attention layers retained. Conversion + tests included. PR #31779
  • MageVL-Cowork multimodal support in progress, including RoPE work; also flags a Metal set_prec bug in kernel_mul_mm_f32_f32 / kernel_mul_mm_f16_f32. PR #31819
  • External PLE (engram) shard loading — new --shard argument to load PLE files from a separate GGUF, with conversion support for PLE-less and PLE-only GGUFs. PR #31185
  • Hexagon: CONV_3D support sharing the CONV_2D op path, plus conv_2d optimizations. PR #31814
  • OpenCL: repeat now supported for f16, i32, i16, bf16. PR #31782
  • WebGPU: batched tensor API get_tensor_n / set_tensor_n. PR #31473
  • NVFP4 quantization on Blackwell (closed PR #23572) — CUDA-native FP4 with Blackwell MMA; claimed Q3_K-tier accuracy at Q4_0 size. PR #23572
  • Multi-GPU Metal: one backend device per physical GPU with cross-device copy guard (eGPU / multi-GPU Macs). PR #28568

4. Performance & Optimization

  • Gemma 4 E2B/E4B prefill "massive gains" — drops unused prompt tokens before KV-shared layers, avoiding compute on layers that don't contribute to KV. Merged/ready. PR #31356
  • Hexagon: fused post-norm residual add into RMS_NORM_MUL — removes one op launch and one DDR activation round-trip per attention/FFN block (×2 per layer) for Gemma-family models. PR #31822
  • KleidiAI SME2 kernels for CPU flash attention (ARM) — routes eligible FLASH_ATTN_EXT QK/AV tile products through F32 SME2 kernels. PR #29394
  • OpenCL small-n GEMV variants for dense q8_0 and MoE q4_k/q5_1 to improve speculative-decoding verification. PR #31831
  • Vulkan readonly decodeBuf declarations — no measured gain yet; expected in future driver versions. PR #31833
  • Known gap: offloaded-MoE prefill leaves GPU idle on serial expert H2D copies (single-GPU -ncmoe, RTX 3060 12GB). Issue #25859
  • Known gap: Vulkan FA SCALAR fallback causes O(N²) PP degradation and device loss on Intel Arc B580/ANV. Issue #27638

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. Vulkan KHR_coopmat nondeterminism — Intel Arc Pro B70 (BMG G31, Mesa 26.2.5): different output on every call for identical input with a BERT-style model, F16 and Q8_0, coopmat enabled by default. No fix PR referenced. Issue #31560
  2. RAM-backed prompt cache cross-contamination (#27148): --cache-ram / --cache-idle-slots (both default-on) can restore KV from an unrelated finished conversation into a fresh slot under concurrent load — a correctness and potential data-isolation issue for multi-tenant servers. Issue #27148
  3. CUDA illegal memory access, Gemma 4 31B + draft-mtp after KV rollback/clear (checkpoint restore or full re-process); no crash with MTP off. Issue #31077
  4. CUDA illegal memory access on GLM-5.3-Flash long prefill at -ub 2048 (Blackwell sm_120, PR branch only). Issue #28282
  5. gfx1201 head-size-256 WMMA FA dispatch threshold too low — ~20% speculative-decoding regression since #28102 on Radeon. Issue #28867
  6. draft-dflash abort in post_decode seq_rm on hybrid Qwen3.8-27B with --parallel 8. Issue #31656
  7. SYCL dual Arc B60 --cpu-moe -sm layer stalls with large MoE cache; ~100–1000× slower than single-GPU. Issue #31510
  8. Spec decode regression with MTP n-max > 1 and -np > 1 on Vulkan. Issue #27544
  9. CPU backend falsely reports MUL_MAT support for types lacking vec_dot kernels (Q8_1, Q8_K, I64, I32) — NULL function pointer deref. Fix PR open. PR #31832
  10. Minor: memory leak report on aarch64/CUDA. Issue #27725

Also relevant: #30683 fixes checkpoint reuse copying and a --cache-reuse bug where deleting a mid-prompt chunk could restore a checkpoint containing deleted tokens (wrong output).

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Treat the RAM prompt cache as suspect in multi-user setups until #27148 is resolved. If you run llama-server with defaults under concurrent load, consider disabling --cache-idle-slots or isolating slots per tenant to avoid cross-conversation KV bleed.
  • Disable Vulkan coopmat on Intel Arc B-series if you need deterministic outputs (classification, routing, eval harnesses) — #31560 shows per-call variance with defaults on.
  • MoE cache semantics changed in b12170. Re-benchmark --n-cpu-moe workloads; eviction behaviour under the new ClassLRU differs from prior LRFU-only logic.
  • Gemma 4 deployments get meaningful prefill wins from #31356 — worth pulling for long-prompt RAG/agent workloads.
  • Speculative decoding verification is being actively tuned across OpenCL (#31831) and Vulkan (#27544 regression). If you depend on draft models for latency, pin your backend build and test MTP n-max > 1 explicitly.
  • Kimi-K3.1-Pro is now servable out of the box, including conversion — relevant if you're evaluating DSA-style sparse attention for cost reduction on long-context agent traces.
